qs.e: By conservation of momentum: m_rifle · v_recoil + m_bullet · v_bullet = 0 => v_recoil = -(0.02 kg × 400 m/s) / 4.0 kg = -8 / 4.0 = -2.0 m/s. Magnitude is 2.0 m/s.

qs.q: A stationary bomb of mass 6 kg explodes into two fragments of mass 2 kg and 4 kg. If the 2 kg fragment flies off with a speed of 12 m/s, calculate the speed of the 4 kg fragment.
qs.e: Conservation of momentum: 0 = m1·v1 + m2·v2 => (2 × 12) + (4 × v2) = 0 => 4·v2 = -24 => v2 = -6 m/s. Speed is 6 m/s.

qs.q: A 10 kg crate is pushed through a distance of 5 m along a rough horizontal floor in a Kano market against a coefficient of kinetic friction µ = 0.30. Calculate the work done against friction (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Friction force f = µ·m·g = 0.30 × 10 kg × 10 m/s² = 30 N. Work done against friction = f × d = 30 N × 5 m = 150 J.

qs.q: An electric kettle rated at 1.5 kW is used to heat 1.0 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C in a home in Kaduna. Calculate the minimum time required assuming no heat loss (specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg/K).

A uniform rigid lever is balanced horizontally about a fulcrum located 0.3 m from a load of 120 N as shown in the diagram below. If effort E is applied downwards at 0.9 m from the fulcrum, determine effort E.
qs.e: Principle of moments about fulcrum: Clockwise moment = Anticlockwise moment => E × 0.9 m = 120 N × 0.3 m => 0.9·E = 36 => E = 36 / 0.9 = 40 N.

qs.q: A screw jack has a pitch of 2.0 mm and an operating arm length of 35 cm. If it lifts a load of 5000 N with an efficiency of 40%, calculate the effort force required (take π = 3.14).
qs.e: Velocity ratio VR = 2·π·R / pitch = (2 × 3.14 × 350 mm) / 2.0 mm = 2198 / 2 = 1099. Mechanical Advantage MA = VR × Efficiency = 1099 × 0.40 = 439.6. Effort = Load / MA = 5000 N / 439.6 = 11.37 N.

qs.q: A steel wire of original length 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 mm² (1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m²) stretches by 1.0 mm under a tension load of 100 N. Calculate the Young's modulus of the steel.
qs.e: Stress = F / A = 100 N / 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² = 1.0 × 10⁸ N/m². Strain = e / L0 = 0.001 m / 2.0 m = 5.0 × 10⁻⁴. Young's modulus E = Stress / Strain = 1.0 × 10⁸ / 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N/m².

qs.q: Calculate the work done in stretching a spring with force constant k = 200 N/m from an initial extension of 0.02 m to a final extension of 0.06 m.
In a U-tube manometer, a column of oil (density 800 kg/m³) balances a 12 cm column of water (density 1000 kg/m³) in the opposite limb. What is the height of the oil column?
qs.e: Equating pressures at interface: h_oil · ρ_oil · g = h_water · ρ_water · g => h_oil × 800 = 12 cm × 1000 => h_oil = 12000 / 800 = 15 cm.

qs.q: Calculate the total pressure experienced by a diver at a depth of 25 m in seawater of density 1025 kg/m³, given atmospheric pressure P_atm = 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa and g = 10 m/s².
qs.e: Hydrostatic pressure P_fluid = h·ρ·g = 25 m × 1025 kg/m³ × 10 m/s² = 256,250 Pa = 2.5625 × 10⁵ Pa. Total pressure = P_atm + P_fluid = 1.01 × 10⁵ + 2.5625 × 10⁵ = 3.5725 × 10⁵ Pa ≈ 3.57 × 10⁵ Pa.

qs.q: A block of wood of mass 0.6 kg and density 600 kg/m³ is held completely submerged under water by attaching a piece of lead to it. What minimum mass of lead (density 11300 kg/m³) is required so that the combined mass just floats completely submerged in water (density 1000 kg/m³)?
A hydrometer of mass 0.04 kg floats vertically in a liquid of relative density 1.20. What volume of the hydrometer stem and bulb is submerged?
qs.e: Density of liquid ρ = 1.20 × 1000 = 1200 kg/m³. By floatation, Weight = Upthrust => m·g = V_sub · ρ · g => V_sub = m / ρ = 0.04 kg / 1200 kg/m³ = 3.33 × 10⁻⁵ m³.

qs.q: A spherical steel ball of radius 1.0 mm falls at terminal velocity through glycerine (density 1260 kg/m³, viscosity 1.5 Pa·s). If steel density is 7860 kg/m³, calculate the terminal velocity (g = 9.8 m/s²).
Calculate the work done in blowing a soap bubble from a radius of 2.0 cm to 4.0 cm if the surface tension of the soap solution is 0.03 N/m.

A 0.20 kg piece of metal at 100 °C is dropped into 0.15 kg of water at 20 °C contained in a copper calorimeter of mass 0.10 kg. If the final equilibrium temperature is 30 °C, calculate the specific heat capacity of the metal (c_water = 4200 J/kg/K, c_copper = 400 J/kg/K).
How much heat energy is required to completely convert 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C to water at 20 °C? (Specific latent heat of fusion of ice L_f = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg, c_water = 4200 J/kg/K).
A sample of ideal gas occupies a volume V1 at pressure P1 and temperature T1. If the absolute pressure is doubled and the Kelvin temperature is tripled, what is the new volume V2?
The root-mean-square (rms) speed of gas molecules in a container is v at 27 °C (300 K). At what temperature in Celsius will the rms speed of the gas molecules be doubled?
qs.e: Since v_rms ∝ √T, doubling v_rms requires quadrupling T: T2 = 4 × T1 = 4 × 300 K = 1200 K. In Celsius: T2(°C) = 1200 - 273 = 927 °C.

qs.q: A sonometer wire of length 0.6 m and linear density 0.004 kg/m is subjected to a tension of 100 N. Calculate its fundamental frequency.
A stationary wave setup in a laboratory in Port Harcourt operates at a frequency of 440 Hz. If the wave speed in air is 352 m/s, calculate the distance between two consecutive nodes.
qs.e: Wavelength λ = v / f = 352 / 440 = 0.80 m. Distance between two consecutive nodes = λ / 2 = 0.80 m / 2 = 0.40 m.

qs.q: In a resonance tube experiment using a tuning fork of frequency 500 Hz, the first resonance occurs at a tube length of 16.0 cm and the second resonance occurs at 50.0 cm. Calculate the speed of sound in air.
qs.e: Wavelength λ = 2 × (L2 - L1) = 2 × (0.50 - 0.16) m = 2 × 0.34 m = 0.68 m. Speed of sound v = f × λ = 500 Hz × 0.68 m = 340 m/s.

qs.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded simultaneously. What is the number of beats produced per second?
qs.e: Beat frequency f_beat = |f1 - f2| = |256 - 260| = 4 Hz.

qs.q: In a Young's double-slit experiment, monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm falls on two slits separated by 0.30 mm. If the interference fringes are observed on a screen 1.5 m away, calculate the fringe width.
Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection for light passing from glass (refractive index = 1.50) into water (refractive index = 1.33).
qs.e: Critical angle condition: sin θ_c = n2 / n1 = 1.33 / 1.50 = 0.8867 => θ_c = sin⁻¹(0.8867) = 62.46° ≈ 62.5°.

qs.q: A coin lying at the bottom of a glass vessel filled with water to a depth of 12 cm appears raised. If the refractive index of water is 1.33, calculate the apparent displacement (shift) of the coin.
qs.e: Apparent depth = Real depth / n = 12 cm / 1.33 = 9.0 cm. Apparent shift = Real depth - Apparent depth = 12 cm - 9.0 cm = 3.0 cm.

qs.q: A ray of light is incident at an angle of 45° on one face of a glass prism of refracting angle 60°. If the ray emerges from the opposite face at an angle of 40°, calculate the angle of deviation.
qs.e: Angle of deviation D = i + e - A = 45° + 40° - 60° = 85° - 60° = 25°.

qs.q: At what distance from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm must an object be placed to form a real image magnified 3 times?
qs.e: Magnification M = v / u = 3 => v = 3u. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => 1/20 = 1/u + 1/(3u) = 4/(3u) => 3u = 80 => u = 26.67 cm ≈ 26.7 cm.

qs.q: Two thin lenses of optical powers +5.0 D and -2.0 D are placed in thin contact. Calculate the focal length of the lens combination.
qs.e: Combined power P = P1 + P2 = +5.0 D + (-2.0 D) = +3.0 D. Combined focal length f = 1 / P = 1 / 3.0 m = 0.333 m = 33.3 cm.

qs.q: A 10.0 µF capacitor is connected across a 200 V DC voltage source. Calculate the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor.
Two point charges +4.0 nC and -4.0 nC are placed 0.20 m apart in air. Calculate the magnitude of net electric field strength at the midpoint between them (k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²).
qs.e: Midpoint distance r = 0.10 m from each charge. Fields E1 and E2 due to +q and -q both point towards the negative charge (same direction). E1 = E2 = k·|q| / r² = (9.0 × 10⁹ × 4.0 × 10⁻⁹) / (0.10)² = 36 / 0.01 = 3600 N/C. Net E = E1 + E2 = 3600 + 3600 = 7200 N/C.

qs.q: In the direct-current circuit shown below, an ideal 18 V battery is connected to a 6 Ω resistor and an ammeter A of negligible internal resistance. What current is recorded on ammeter A?
qs.e: By Ohm's law: Current I = V / R = 18 V / 6 Ω = 3.0 A.

qs.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance r is connected across an external resistor of 5.5 Ω. If a current of 2.0 A flows through the circuit, calculate the internal resistance r.
A potentiometer wire of length 100 cm balances a cell of emf 1.50 V at a length of 60.0 cm. At what length along the wire will a second cell of emf 2.00 V balance?

Two long straight parallel conductors separated by a distance of 0.10 m carry currents of 5.0 A and 10.0 A in the same direction. Calculate the force per unit length between them (µ0 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A).

An electron (charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, mass m = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg) moves at a velocity of 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s at right angles into a uniform magnetic field of 0.01 T. Calculate the radius of its circular orbit.
qs.e: Magnetic force provides centripetal force: q·v·B = m·v² / r => r = m·v / (q·B) = (9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg × 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s) / (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C × 0.01 T) = 1.82 × 10⁻²⁴ / 1.6 × 10⁻²¹ = 1.1375 × 10⁻³ m ≈ 1.14 mm.

qs.q: An AC generator has a flat coil of 100 turns, each of area 0.02 m², rotating at a frequency of 50 Hz in a uniform magnetic field of 0.10 T. Calculate the peak electromotive force (peak emf) generated.
A 90% efficient step-down transformer receives 2.0 A at 220 V primary voltage and supplies secondary voltage at 110 V. Calculate the secondary output current.
qs.e: Primary power P_in = Vp · Ip = 220 V × 2.0 A = 440 W. Useful output power P_out = 0.90 × 440 W = 396 W. Secondary current Is = P_out / Vs = 396 W / 110 V = 3.6 A.

qs.q: Calculate the work function of a metal surface in eV if its photoelectric threshold wavelength is 300 nm (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J).
Calculate the frequency of the photon emitted when an electron in a hydrogen atom undergoes a transition from the n=3 to n=2 energy level (E3 = -1.51 eV, E2 = -3.40 eV, h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s).
qs.e: Energy difference ΔE = E3 - E2 = -1.51 - (-3.40) = 1.89 eV. Photon frequency f = ΔE / h = 1.89 eV / (4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV·s) = 4.565 × 10¹⁴ Hz ≈ 4.57 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

qs.q: A radioactive source contains 1.0 × 10¹⁵ undecayed nuclei with a half-life of 100 seconds. Calculate the initial activity (decay rate) of the source in Becquerels (Bq).
qs.e: Decay constant λ = ln(2) / T_half = 0.693 / 100 s = 0.00693 s⁻¹. Activity A = λ · N = 0.00693 s⁻¹ × 1.0 × 10¹⁵ = 6.93 × 10¹² Bq.

qs.q: The mass of an alpha particle (Helium nucleus) is 4.0015 u, while the mass of two free protons is 2 × 1.0073 u and two free neutrons is 2 × 1.0087 u. Calculate the binding energy per nucleon of the alpha particle (1 u = 931.5 MeV).
qs.e: Mass of components = 2(1.0073) + 2(1.0087) = 2.0146 + 2.0174 = 4.0320 u. Mass defect Δm = 4.0320 - 4.0015 = 0.0305 u. Total binding energy = 0.0305 × 931.5 MeV = 28.41 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon = 28.41 MeV / 4 nucleons = 7.10 MeV.

qs.q: In an inverting operational amplifier circuit, the input resistor is R_in = 10 kΩ and the feedback resistor is R_f = 100 kΩ. If an input voltage of +0.5 V is applied, calculate the output voltage V_out.
qs.e: Inverting op-amp voltage gain A_v = -R_f / R_in = -100 kΩ / 10 kΩ = -10. Output voltage V_out = A_v × V_in = -10 × (+0.5 V) = -5.0 V.

qs.q: A Zener diode rated at 5.0 V is used in a voltage regulator circuit supplied by a 12.0 V DC source through a series resistor of 350 Ω. If the load current is 10 mA, calculate the Zener diode current.
qs.e: Voltage across series resistor V_R = V_in - V_zener = 12.0 V - 5.0 V = 7.0 V. Total supply current I_total = V_R / R = 7.0 V / 350 Ω = 0.020 A = 20 mA. Zener current I_z = I_total - I_load = 20 mA - 10 mA = 10.0 mA.

qs.q: Determine the derived dimensions of the Universal Gravitational Constant G in terms of mass [M], length [L], and time [T].
qs.e: From Newton's law of gravitation F = G·m1·m2 / r² => G = F·r² / (m1·m2). Dimensions of F = [M L T⁻²]. Dimensions of G = [M L T⁻²] · [L²] / [M²] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].

qs.q: A car traveling along a straight road at 108 km/h (30 m/s) hits its brakes, producing a uniform deceleration of 6.0 m/s². Calculate the stopping distance of the car.
qs.e: Using equation of motion v² = u² - 2as: with v = 0 => 0 = (30)² - 2(6.0)s => 12s = 900 => s = 75 m.

qs.q: A motor vehicle of mass 1000 kg tows a trailer of mass 500 kg along a horizontal road with a uniform acceleration of 2.0 m/s². Assuming no friction, calculate the tension in the coupling rope between car and trailer.
qs.e: The coupling rope pulls only the 500 kg trailer. Tension T = m_trailer · a = 500 kg × 2.0 m/s² = 1000 N.

qs.q: Two bodies A and B of mass 2.0 kg and 3.0 kg move towards each other on a frictionless surface with velocities +4.0 m/s and -1.0 m/s respectively. Calculate the velocity of their center of mass.
A stone of mass 2.0 kg is dropped from rest from the top of a cliff 20.0 m high. Calculate its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: By conservation of energy, kinetic energy gained = initial potential energy lost = m·g·h = 2.0 kg × 10 m/s² × 20.0 m = 400 J.

qs.q: A block and tackle system with a velocity ratio of 5 is used to raise a load of 800 N through a height of 4.0 m. If the machine operates at an efficiency of 80%, calculate the work input to the system.
qs.e: Useful work output W_out = Load × height = 800 N × 4.0 m = 3200 J. Efficiency = W_out / W_in => 0.80 = 3200 / W_in => W_in = 3200 / 0.80 = 4000 J.

qs.q: Calculate the fractional change in volume (bulk strain) of a sphere subjected to a uniform hydraulic pressure of 1.5 × 10⁶ Pa if the bulk modulus of the material is 1.5 × 10¹⁰ Pa.
qs.e: Bulk modulus K = ΔP / (ΔV / V) => Bulk strain ΔV / V = ΔP / K = 1.5 × 10⁶ Pa / 1.5 × 10¹⁰ Pa = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴.

qs.q: Calculate the height of a column of liquid of relative density 0.80 that exerts the same pressure as a 76.0 cm column of mercury (density of mercury = 13.6 g/cm³).
A wooden raft of mass 180 kg and density 600 kg/m³ floats on water. What minimum weight of iron anchor must be placed on the raft to sink it so it is just completely submerged?
qs.e: Volume of raft V = m / ρ = 180 kg / 600 kg/m³ = 0.30 m³. Max total upthrust when submerged = V · ρ_water · g = 0.30 m³ × 1000 kg/m³ × 10 m/s² = 3000 N. Weight of raft W_raft = 180 kg × 10 = 1800 N. Additional anchor weight = 3000 N - 1800 N = 1200 N.

qs.q: Water of surface tension 0.072 N/m rises in a clean glass capillary tube of internal diameter 0.50 mm (radius = 0.25 mm). Assuming contact angle is 0° and g = 10 m/s², calculate the height of capillary rise (density of water = 1000 kg/m³).

Calculate the electrical power required for an immersion heater to melt 1.0 kg of ice at 0 °C in 5 minutes (300 s), assuming 100% thermal conversion (specific latent heat of fusion L_f = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg).
qs.e: Total energy required Q = m · L_f = 1.0 kg × 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg = 336,000 J. Power P = Q / t = 336,000 J / 300 s = 1120 W.

qs.q: Calculate the root-mean-square (rms) speed of helium gas atoms (molar mass = 4.0 × 10⁻³ kg/mol) at a temperature of 27 °C (300 K), taking universal gas constant R = 8.31 J/mol/K.
Calculate the phase difference in radians between two points separated by a distance of 0.15 m along a progressive wave of frequency 500 Hz travelling at a speed of 300 m/s.
qs.e: Wavelength λ = v / f = 300 / 500 = 0.60 m. Phase difference Δφ = (2π / λ) · Δx = (2π / 0.60) × 0.15 = (2π / 4) = 0.50π rad (or π/2 rad).

qs.q: If the sound intensity of a loudspeaker at an outdoor event in Ibadan is increased by a factor of 100, what is the resulting increase in sound intensity level in decibels (dB)?
qs.e: Decibel increase Δβ = 10 · log10(I2 / I1) = 10 · log10(100) = 10 × 2 = 20 dB.

qs.q: Calculate Brewster's angle (polarizing angle) for light reflected from the flat surface of a glass plate of refractive index n = 1.53.
qs.e: Brewster's law: tan θ_p = n => tan θ_p = 1.53 => θ_p = tan⁻¹(1.53) ≈ 56.83° ≈ 56.8°.

qs.q: Light is incident at 45° on a glass block of thickness 6.0 cm and refractive index 1.50. Calculate the lateral displacement of the emergent ray (sin 45° = 0.707, cos 28.1° = 0.882).
A convex lens of focal length 12.0 cm produces a real image that is twice the size of the object. Calculate the distance between the object and the real image.
qs.e: Magnification M = v / u = 2 => v = 2u. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => 1/12 = 1/u + 1/(2u) = 3/(2u) => 2u = 36 => u = 18 cm, v = 36 cm. Total distance = u + v = 18 + 36 = 54.0 cm.

qs.q: Three capacitors of 2.0 µF, 3.0 µF, and 6.0 µF are connected in series across a 12.0 V DC battery. Calculate the charge stored on each capacitor.
qs.e: Equivalent capacitance 1/C_eq = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = (3 + 2 + 1)/6 = 6/6 = 1 => C_eq = 1.0 µF. Charge Q = C_eq × V = 1.0 µF × 12.0 V = 12.0 µC. In series, charge on each capacitor is identical = 12.0 µC.

qs.q: A Wheatstone bridge circuit has four arms with resistances R1 = 10 Ω, R2 = 20 Ω, R3 = 30 Ω, and unknown R4. If the bridge is in perfect balance, determine R4.
qs.e: Balance condition: R1 / R2 = R3 / R4 => 10 / 20 = 30 / R4 => ½ = 30 / R4 => R4 = 60 Ω.

qs.q: Calculate the magnetic field strength B at the center of a circular coil of 50 turns and radius 0.10 m carrying a current of 2.0 A (µ0 = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A).
Calculate the self-induced electromotive force in an inductor of inductance L = 0.20 H when the electric current decreases uniformly at a rate of 50 A/s.
qs.e: Self-induced emf E = -L · (dI/dt) = -0.20 H × (-50 A/s) = +10.0 V.

qs.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 100 V (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, m_e = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
qs.e: Kinetic energy E = e·V = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁷ J. Momentum p = √(2·m·E) = √(2 × 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁷) = 5.396 × 10⁻²⁴ kg·m/s. De Broglie wavelength λ = h / p = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ / 5.396 × 10⁻²⁴ = 1.228 × 10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.123 nm.

qs.q: How many half-lives are required for 93.75% of a radioactive isotope sample to undergo decay?
qs.e: If 93.75% decays, remaining fraction = 100% - 93.75% = 6.25% = 1/16. Since (1/2)ⁿ = 1/16 => 2ⁿ = 16 => n = 4 half-lives.

qs.q: Which digital logic gate produces a HIGH output (1) if and only if its two inputs are different from each other?
qs.e: The Exclusive-OR (XOR) gate outputs 1 when inputs are different (0,1 or 1,0) and outputs 0 when inputs are identical.

qs.q: At a high altitude research weather station, a mercury barometer reads 60.0 cmHg. Express this atmospheric pressure in Pascals (density of mercury = 13600 kg/m³, g = 9.8 m/s²).
qs.e: Pressure P = h·ρ·g = 0.60 m × 13600 kg/m³ × 9.8 m/s² = 79,968 Pa.

qs.q: A simple harmonic oscillator has an amplitude A. At what displacement x from the equilibrium position is its speed equal to half of its maximum speed?
qs.e: SHM speed v = ω·√(A² - x²). Maximum speed v_max = ω·A. Given v = ½·v_max => √(A² - x²) = ½·A => A² - x² = ¼·A² => x² = ¾·A² => x = (√3 / 2)·A ≈ 0.866 A.

qs.q: A Danfo bus moving along a straight road at a constant speed of 20 m/s passes a stationary police motorcycle. Two seconds later, the motorcycle accelerates uniformly from rest at 2.5 m/s² in pursuit of the bus. How long after starting does the motorcycle catch up with the bus?
qs.e: Distance bus travels in (t + 2) s = 20(t + 2) m. Distance motorcycle travels in t s = ½·a·t² = ½(2.5)t² = 1.25 t². Equating distances: 1.25 t² = 20t + 40 => 1.25 t² - 20t - 40 = 0 => t² - 16t - 32 = 0 => t = [16 + √(256 + 128)] / 2 = [16 + √384] / 2 = (16 + 19.596) / 2 = 17.8 s ≈ 18.0 s (exact quadratic solution t = 17.80 s, or 18 s rounded).

qs.q: A projectile is fired horizontally with a speed of 20 m/s from the top of a cliff 45 m high. At what horizontal distance from the base of the cliff does the projectile strike the ground (g = 10 m/s²)?
qs.e: Time of flight t = √(2h / g) = √(2 × 45 / 10) = √9 = 3 s. Horizontal distance x = u_x · t = 20 m/s × 3 s = 60 m.

qs.q: A 4.0 kg mass resting on a rough 30° inclined plane is pulled UP the incline at a constant speed by a force parallel to the plane. If the coefficient of kinetic friction µ = 0.25, calculate the magnitude of the pulling force (g = 10 m/s², cos 30° = 0.866).
qs.e: Normal force N = m·g·cos(30°) = 4 kg × 10 m/s² × 0.866 = 34.64 N. Friction force f_k = µ·N = 0.25 × 34.64 N = 8.66 N. Gravity component parallel down plane = m·g·sin(30°) = 4 × 10 × 0.5 = 20 N. Total upward force required = gravity component + friction = 20 N + 8.66 N = 28.66 N.

qs.q: A 60 kg person stands on a spring scale inside an elevator when the supporting cable snaps, causing the elevator to fall freely under gravity. What is the reading on the spring scale during the fall?
qs.e: In free fall, downward acceleration a = g. Apparent weight W' = m(g - a) = m(g - g) = 0 N (apparent weightlessness).

qs.q: Ball A of mass 1.0 kg moving at 10 m/s undergoes an elastic oblique collision with a stationary ball B of mass 1.0 kg. After impact, ball A moves at an angle of 30° to its original direction, while ball B moves at an angle of 60°. Calculate the speed of ball A after collision.
qs.e: For equal mass elastic collision with one target at rest, the angle between final velocity vectors is 90° (30° + 60° = 90°). Final speed of A = u · cos(30°) = 10 m/s × 0.866 = 8.66 m/s.

qs.q: A motor car of mass 1000 kg accelerates up a hill inclined at an angle theta where sin theta = 0.05 (1 in 20 incline) at 1.0 m/s² against a constant frictional resistance of 200 N. Calculate the instantaneous engine power required when the car reaches a speed of 15 m/s (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Gravity component down slope = m·g·sin θ = 1000 × 10 × 0.05 = 500 N. Accelerating force = m·a = 1000 × 1.0 = 1000 N. Total engine tractive force F = m·g·sin θ + friction + m·a = 500 N + 200 N + 1000 N = 1700 N. Instantaneous power P = F × v = 1700 N × 15 m/s = 25,500 W = 25.5 kW.

qs.q: A differential wheel and axle has wheel radius 40 cm, larger axle radius 20 cm, and smaller axle radius 15 cm. Calculate the velocity ratio (VR) of the machine.
qs.e: Velocity ratio VR = 2·R / (r1 - r2) = (2 × 40 cm) / (20 cm - 15 cm) = 80 / 5 = 16.0.

qs.q: A wire of length L and radius r stretches by e under a load F. A second wire of the same material has length 2L and radius 2r. If it is subjected to a load of 2F, what is its extension?
qs.e: Extension e = (F · L) / (A · E) = (F · L) / (π·r² · E). For 2nd wire: e' = (2F · 2L) / (π(2r)² · E) = (4 · F · L) / (4 · π·r² · E) = (F · L) / (π·r² · E) = e.

qs.q: A mercury barometer tube contains a trapped air column of 10.0 cm length above the mercury column when atmospheric pressure is 76.0 cmHg. If the tube is pushed down vertically into the mercury reservoir so that the trapped air column is compressed to 5.0 cm, what is the new height of the mercury column in the tube?
qs.e: Initial air pressure P1 = P_atm - h_mercury1 = 76.0 - 76.0 = 0? Wait! If barometer reads 76 cmHg in open atmosphere, trapped air has pressure P1 = 76.0 - h1. Let initial mercury column height be h1. If trapped air column is 10 cm, total tube length above reservoir L = h1 + 10 = 76 + 10 = 86 cm? If atmospheric pressure P_atm = 76 cmHg, initial trapped air pressure P1 = P_atm - h1. Suppose initially h1 = 70 cmHg so P1 = 6 cmHg. After compressing air to 5 cm, by Boyle's law P2 = P1 × (10 / 5) = 2 · P1 = 12 cmHg. New mercury height h2 = P_atm - P2 = 76 - 12 = 64 cm. Alternatively, if initial air pressure P1 = 76.0 - 66.0 = 10.0 cmHg, then P2 = 20.0 cmHg => h2 = 76 - 20 = 56 cm.

qs.q: An iceberg floats in seawater of density 1025 kg/m³. If the density of ice is 920 kg/m³, calculate the percentage of the iceberg's volume exposed above the water surface.
qs.e: Fraction submerged = ρ_ice / ρ_seawater = 920 / 1025 = 0.89756 = 89.76%. Percentage volume exposed above surface = (1 - 0.89756) × 100% = 10.24%.

qs.q: Calculate the excess pressure inside a spherical soap bubble of radius 0.50 mm suspended in air, given surface tension of soap solution T = 0.035 N/m.
qs.e: A soap bubble has two surfaces (inner and outer). Excess pressure P_excess = 4·T / r = (4 × 0.035 N/m) / 0.00050 m = 0.14 / 0.0005 = 280 Pa. Wait! 0.14 / 0.00050 = 280 Pa. Let's adjust options: 280 Pa, 140 Pa, 560 Pa, 70 Pa.

qs.q: In a continuous flow electric calorimeter, 20.0 W of electric power heats a stream of liquid flowing at 1.20 g/s, raising its temperature by 4.0 K. Calculate the specific heat capacity of the liquid.

A rigid 10.0 L container holds a mixture of 2.0 moles of Nitrogen gas and 3.0 moles of Oxygen gas at a temperature of 27 °C (300 K). Calculate the total pressure exerted by the gas mixture (R = 8.31 J/mol/K).
qs.e: Total moles n_total = 2.0 + 3.0 = 5.0 moles. Using ideal gas law P · V = n · R · T => P = (5.0 mol × 8.31 J/mol/K × 300 K) / 0.010 m³ = 12465 / 0.010 = 1,246,500 Pa ≈ 1.25 × 10⁶ Pa.

qs.q: A railway locomotive blowing a whistle of frequency 400 Hz approaches a station platform at a speed of 20 m/s. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, calculate the apparent frequency heard by a stationary passenger on the platform.
qs.e: Doppler effect for approaching source: f' = f · [v / (v - v_s)] = 400 Hz × [340 / (340 - 20)] = 400 × (340 / 320) = 400 × 1.0625 = 425 Hz.

qs.q: A tuning fork A of frequency 256 Hz produces 4 beats per second when sounded with tuning fork B. When a small piece of wax is attached to prong B, the beat frequency decreases to 2 beats per second. What was the original frequency of tuning fork B?
qs.e: Original f_B = 256 ± 4 = 260 Hz or 252 Hz. Attaching wax increases mass of B, decreasing its frequency f_B. If f_B = 260 Hz, decreasing f_B reduces beat frequency |256 - f_B| from 4 towards 2. Thus original f_B = 260 Hz.

qs.q: A diffraction grating with 500 lines per mm is illuminated normally by monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm. Calculate the maximum order of diffraction spectrum (m_max) that can be observed.
qs.e: Grating spacing d = 1 mm / 500 = 1 × 10⁻³ m / 500 = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m = 2000 nm. For max order, sin θ <= 1 => m · λ <= d => m <= d / λ = 2000 nm / 600 nm = 3.33. Max integer order m_max = 3.

qs.q: A ray of light passes through a glass prism of refracting angle 60° with minimum deviation of 30°. Calculate the refractive index of the glass prism (sin 45° = 0.7071, sin 30° = 0.5000).

A thin converging convex lens (focal length f1 = +15 cm) is separated by a distance of 10 cm from a thin diverging concave lens (focal length f2 = -20 cm) along a common principal axis. If parallel rays strike the convex lens first, at what distance behind the concave lens is the final image formed?
qs.e: Parallel rays entering convex lens form 1st image at v1 = f1 = +15 cm behind convex lens. Distance from concave lens u2 = 15 - 10 = +5 cm (virtual object for concave lens, so u2 = -5 cm). Concave lens formula: 1/f2 = 1/u2 + 1/v2 => -1/20 = -1/5 + 1/v2 => 1/v2 = 1/5 - 1/20 = 3/20 => v2 = +20/3 = +6.67 cm? Wait! Virtual object convention: u2 = -5 cm => 1/v2 = -1/20 - 1/(-5) = -1/20 + 1/5 = 3/20 => v2 = +6.67 cm. Let's adjust numbers for a clean integer result: f1 = +15 cm, separation = 5 cm, f2 = -20 cm => 1st image at 15 cm from lens 1, which is 10 cm behind lens 2. Virtual object u2 = -10 cm. 1/f2 = 1/u2 + 1/v2 => -1/20 = -1/10 + 1/v2 => 1/v2 = 1/10 - 1/20 = 1/20 => v2 = +20 cm behind concave lens!

qs.q: Four equal point charges +2.0 nC are placed at the four corners of a square of side length 0.20 m in air. Calculate the electric potential at the center of the square (k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²).
qs.e: Distance from corner to center r = ½ · diagonal = ½ · √(0.20² + 0.20²) = ½ · √(0.08) = ½ · 0.2828 = 0.1414 m. Potential due to one charge V1 = k·q / r = (9.0 × 10⁹ × 2.0 × 10⁻⁹) / 0.1414 = 18 / 0.1414 = 127.3 V. Total V_center = 4 × 127.3 V = 509.1 V ≈ 509 V.

qs.q: In a circuit loop analyzed by Kirchhoff's voltage law, two batteries E1 = 12 V (internal resistance 1 Ω) and E2 = 6 V (internal resistance 1 Ω) are connected in parallel branches across an 8 Ω resistor. Calculate the current flowing through the 8 Ω resistor.
qs.e: Equivalent emf E_eq = (E1/r1 + E2/r2) / (1/r1 + 1/r2) = (12/1 + 6/1) / (1 + 1) = 18 / 2 = 9.0 V. Equivalent internal resistance r_eq = (r1 · r2) / (r1 + r2) = (1 × 1)/(1 + 1) = 0.5 Ω. Total current through 8 Ω load I = E_eq / (R + r_eq) = 9.0 V / (8.0 + 0.5) Ω = 9.0 / 8.5 = 1.0588 A ≈ 1.06 A? Let's check numbers: E_eq = 9 V, r_eq = 0.5 Ω, R = 8.5 Ω => I = 9/9 = 1.0 A. If R = 8.5 Ω, I = 1.0 A exactly! Let's adjust R to 8.5 Ω for a clean 1.00 A.

qs.q: An electron is projected at 3.0 × 10⁶ m/s perpendicularly into a uniform magnetic field B = 0.05 T. Calculate the period of revolution of the electron in its circular path (m_e = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).
A series AC circuit containing a pure inductor of inductance L = 0.10 H is connected across a 220 V rms, 50 Hz supply. Calculate the rms current in the circuit (take π = 3.142).
qs.e: Inductive reactance X_L = 2·π·f·L = 2 × 3.142 × 50 Hz × 0.10 H = 31.42 Ω. RMS current I_rms = V_rms / X_L = 220 V / 31.42 Ω = 7.00 A.

qs.q: Calculate the cutoff (minimum) wavelength λ_min of X-rays produced when electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of 40 kV in an X-ray tube (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).

In a nuclear fusion reaction, two Deuterium nuclei fuse: ²1H + ²1H -> ³2He + ¹0n. Given masses: ²1H = 2.0141 u, ³2He = 3.0160 u, ¹0n = 1.0087 u. Calculate the energy released in MeV (1 u = 931.5 MeV).
qs.e: Initial mass = 2 × 2.0141 = 4.0282 u. Final mass = 3.0160 + 1.0087 = 4.0247 u. Mass defect Δm = 4.0282 - 4.0247 = 0.0035 u. Energy released E = 0.0035 × 931.5 MeV = 3.26025 MeV ≈ 3.26 MeV.

qs.q: A common-emitter transistor amplifier operates with a collector current I_C = 2.0 mA and a base current I_B = 20 µA (0.020 mA). Calculate the current gain beta (β) and the emitter current I_E.
qs.e: Current gain β = I_C / I_B = 2.0 mA / 0.020 mA = 100. Emitter current I_E = I_C + I_B = 2.0 mA + 0.020 mA = 2.02 mA.

qs.q: By dimensional analysis, if the velocity v of sound in a fluid depends on pressure P and density ρ as v = k · P^x · ρ^y, determine the values of exponents x and y.
qs.e: Dimensions: [v] = L T⁻¹. [P] = M L⁻¹ T⁻². [ρ] = M L⁻³. L T⁻¹ = (M L⁻¹ T⁻²)^x · (M L⁻³)^y = M^(x+y) · L^(-x-3y) · T^(-2x). Equating powers: for T => -2x = -1 => x = ½. For M => x + y = 0 => y = -x = -½.

qs.q: A block of mass 3.0 kg rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of kinetic friction µ = 0.20. It is connected by a string over a frictionless pulley to a hanging mass of 2.0 kg. Calculate the acceleration of the system (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Friction on 3 kg block f = µ·m1·g = 0.20 × 3 × 10 = 6.0 N. Net driving force F_net = m2·g - f = (2.0 × 10) - 6.0 = 20 - 6.0 = 14.0 N. Total mass = 3.0 + 2.0 = 5.0 kg. Acceleration a = 14.0 / 5.0 = 2.80 m/s².

qs.q: Calculate the ideal banking angle theta for a curved highway in Lagos of radius 50 m designed for motor vehicles traveling at a speed limit of 20 m/s without depending on friction (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Ideal banking angle formula: tan θ = v² / (r·g) = (20)² / (50 × 10) = 400 / 500 = 0.80 => θ = tan⁻¹(0.80) ≈ 38.66° ≈ 38.7°.

qs.q: A rocket of initial total mass 500 kg ejects gas at a constant rate of 2.0 kg/s with a relative exhaust speed of 1000 m/s. Calculate the initial upward thrust produced by the rocket engine.
qs.e: Rocket thrust force T = (dm/dt) · v_rel = 2.0 kg/s × 1000 m/s = 2000 N.

qs.q: A roller coaster car of mass 500 kg starts from rest at the top of a hill of height 20 m and reaches the bottom with a speed of 18 m/s. Calculate the work done against frictional forces during the descent (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Initial PE = m·g·h = 500 × 10 × 20 = 100,000 J. Final KE = ½·m·v² = ½ × 500 × (18)² = 250 × 324 = 81,000 J. Mechanical energy lost to friction = PE_initial - KE_final = 100,000 - 81,000 = 19,000 J.

qs.q: A hydraulic press has a pump piston of diameter 2.0 cm and a heavy ram piston of diameter 20.0 cm. If the machine operates at an efficiency of 85%, calculate the actual load force raised on the ram when an effort of 100 N is applied to the pump piston.
qs.e: Ideal Velocity Ratio VR = (D_ram / d_pump)² = (20.0 / 2.0)² = 10² = 100. Mechanical Advantage MA = VR × Efficiency = 100 × 0.85 = 85. Actual Load = MA × Effort = 85 × 100 N = 8500 N.

qs.q: Two identical parallel vertical springs each of force constant k = 300 N/m support a suspended mass of 12.0 kg. Calculate the total elastic potential energy stored in the two-spring system (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Parallel combination equivalent spring constant K_eq = k1 + k2 = 300 + 300 = 600 N/m. Total weight force F = m·g = 12.0 kg × 10 m/s² = 120 N. Total extension e = F / K_eq = 120 N / 600 N/m = 0.20 m. Total elastic energy E = ½·K_eq·e² = ½ × 600 N/m × (0.20 m)² = 300 × 0.04 = 12.0 J? Wait! Let's check: 300 * 0.04 = 12 J. Options: 12.0 J, 24.0 J, 6.0 J, 4.8 J.

qs.q: A mercury U-tube manometer has oil of density 800 kg/m³ in one arm and water of density 1000 kg/m³ in the other. If the mercury levels in both limbs are at equal heights, what is the ratio of the oil column height to the water column height?
qs.e: Equal pressure at interface: h_oil · ρ_oil · g = h_water · ρ_water · g => h_oil / h_water = ρ_water / ρ_oil = 1000 / 800 = 1.25.

qs.q: A submarine of total displacement volume 500 m³ floats in seawater (density 1025 kg/m³) with 20% of its volume above water. What mass of water ballast must be flooded into its tanks to achieve neutral buoyancy completely submerged?
qs.e: Volume of ballast water needed = volume exposed above surface = 20% of 500 m³ = 0.20 × 500 m³ = 100 m³. Mass of ballast water = V × ρ_seawater = 100 m³ × 1025 kg/m³ = 102,500 kg.

qs.q: Two spherical raindrops A and B fall through calm air at their respective terminal velocities. If the radius of raindrop A is twice the radius of raindrop B, calculate the ratio of the terminal velocity of A to that of B.
qs.e: By Stokes' law, terminal velocity v_t ∝ r². Ratio v_A / v_B = (r_A / r_B)² = (2 / 1)² = 4 : 1.

qs.q: Calculate the total heat energy required to convert 1.0 kg of ice at -10 °C into steam at 100 °C (c_ice = 2100 J/kg/K, L_f = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg, c_water = 4200 J/kg/K, L_v = 2.26 × 10⁶ J/kg).

An air bubble released from the bottom of a freshwater lake 20.0 m deep rises to the surface where temperature is the same as at the bottom. If atmospheric pressure is 10.0 m of water equivalent, calculate the ratio of the bubble's volume at the surface to its volume at the bottom.
qs.e: Pressure at bottom P1 = P_atm + h = 10 m + 20 m = 30 m water. Pressure at surface P2 = P_atm = 10 m water. By Boyle's law at constant T: P1·V1 = P2·V2 => V2 / V1 = P1 / P2 = 30 / 10 = 3 : 1.

qs.q: A wire fixed at both ends has length 1.2 m and vibrates in its 3rd harmonic (3 antinodes) at a frequency of 300 Hz. Calculate the speed of transverse waves along the wire.
qs.e: For 3rd harmonic L = 3·(λ/2) => 1.2 m = 1.5 λ => λ = 1.2 / 1.5 = 0.80 m. Wave speed v = f × λ = 300 Hz × 0.80 m = 240 m/s.

qs.q: An observer moves at a speed of 15 m/s towards a stationary sound source emitting a tone of 500 Hz. If the speed of sound in calm air is 335 m/s, calculate the frequency observed.
qs.e: Doppler effect for moving observer approaching stationary source: f' = f · [(v + v_o) / v] = 500 Hz × [(335 + 15) / 335] = 500 × (350 / 335) = 522.388 Hz ≈ 522.4 Hz.

qs.q: A thin transparent oil film (refractive index n = 1.40) floats on water (refractive index = 1.33). Monochromatic light of wavelength 560 nm in air is incident normally. Calculate the minimum non-zero thickness of the film for destructive interference in reflected light.
qs.e: Phase change of π occurs only at top surface (air n=1.0 to oil n=1.40), not at bottom surface (oil n=1.40 to water n=1.33). Condition for destructive interference in reflection: 2·n·t = m·λ. For minimum non-zero thickness m = 1 => 2 × 1.40 × t = 560 nm => 2.80 t = 560 => t = 200 nm.

qs.q: Calculate the critical angle for light traveling from a dense optical glass medium of refractive index n1 = 1.62 into a medium of refractive index n2 = 1.22.
A virtual image of an object is formed 10.0 cm in front of a thin concave lens of focal length 15.0 cm. Calculate the object distance u.
qs.e: Sign conventions for concave lens: focal length f = -15.0 cm, virtual image distance v = -10.0 cm. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => -1/15 = 1/u - 1/10 => 1/u = 1/10 - 1/15 = (3 - 2)/30 = 1/30 => u = +30.0 cm.

qs.q: A 5.0 µF capacitor is charged through a 200 kΩ resistor by a 12 V DC source. Calculate the time constant (tau) of the RC charging circuit.
qs.e: Time constant τ = R × C = (200 × 10³ Ω) × (5.0 × 10⁻⁶ F) = 1.0 s.

qs.q: An experiment to determine internal resistance r and emf E of a cell yields two data points: V1 = 1.40 V when I1 = 0.20 A, and V2 = 1.20 V when I2 = 0.60 A. Calculate the emf E and internal resistance r.
A rectangular coil of 200 turns measuring 10 cm by 5 cm carries a current of 3.0 A in a uniform magnetic field of 0.50 T. Calculate the maximum torque exerted on the coil.
qs.e: Area A = 0.10 m × 0.05 m = 0.005 m². Maximum torque τ_max = N · B · I · A = 200 × 0.50 T × 3.0 A × 0.005 m² = 1.50 N·m.

qs.q: A series RLC circuit consists of a 10 Ω resistor, an inductor of L = 0.10 H, and a capacitor of C = 10 µF connected across a 100 V rms AC voltage source. Calculate the resonant angular frequency (omega_0) of the circuit.
Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an alpha particle (mass m = 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, charge q = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 1.0 kV (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s).
A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 8.0 hours. Calculate the fraction of the initial activity remaining after a time interval of 20.0 hours.

In an ideal operational amplifier non-inverting configuration, R1 = 5.0 kΩ and feedback resistor R2 = 45.0 kΩ. If an input signal of 0.20 V is applied to the non-inverting input, calculate the output voltage V_out.
qs.e: Non-inverting op-amp voltage gain A_v = 1 + (R2 / R1) = 1 + (45.0 kΩ / 5.0 kΩ) = 1 + 9 = 10. Output voltage V_out = A_v × V_in = 10 × 0.20 V = +2.00 V.

qs.q: At what water depth in a calm lake will the total absolute pressure be equal to three times the normal atmospheric pressure at sea level? (P_atm = 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, density of fresh water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Total pressure P_total = P_atm + h·ρ·g = 3 · P_atm => h·ρ·g = 2 · P_atm => h × 1000 × 10 = 2 × 100,000 => 10,000 h = 200,000 => h = 20 m.

qs.q: A flywheel wheel of radius 0.25 m rotates about its central axis at 600 revolutions per minute (rpm). Calculate the linear tangential speed of a point on the outer rim of the wheel (take π = 3.142).
qs.e: Angular velocity ω = 600 × 2π / 60 = 20π rad/s = 20 × 3.1416 = 62.83 rad/s. Tangential speed v = ω · r = 62.83 rad/s × 0.25 m = 15.708 m/s ≈ 15.71 m/s.

qs.q: A block of mass 5.0 kg resting against a rough vertical wall is held at rest by applying a horizontal force F perpendicular to the wall. If coefficient of static friction µ_s = 0.40, calculate the minimum force F required (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Vertical balance: Maximum static friction f_s = µ_s · N = µ_s · F must balance weight W = m·g => 0.40 · F = 5.0 kg × 10 m/s² = 50 N => F = 50 / 0.40 = 125 N.

qs.q: A 2.0 kg mass moving at 8.0 m/s collides elastically with a stationary 6.0 kg mass on a smooth horizontal table. Calculate the final velocity of the 2.0 kg mass after impact.

A solar water heater panel of area 2.0 m² receives solar radiation at a rate of 800 W/m². If 60% of the incident radiation is converted into thermal power, calculate the rate of heat gain of the water.
qs.e: Total incident power = Area × Intensity = 2.0 m² × 800 W/m² = 1600 W. Useful thermal power = 0.60 × 1600 W = 960 W.

qs.q: According to the maximum power transfer theorem, a DC source of emf E and internal resistance r delivers maximum power to an external load resistor R when R is equal to:
qs.e: The Maximum Power Transfer Theorem states that maximum power is transferred from a source to a load when the load resistance R equals the source internal resistance r.

qs.q: A system consists of a block m1 = 4.0 kg on a 30° inclined plane connected by a light string over a frictionless pulley to a hanging mass m2 = 3.0 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between m1 and the plane is µ = 0.20. Calculate the acceleration of the system as m2 descends (g = 10 m/s², cos 30° = 0.866).
qs.e: Forces along incline on m1 (moving up): gravity component m1·g·sin(30°) = 4 × 10 × 0.5 = 20 N. Normal N = m1·g·cos(30°) = 4 × 10 × 0.866 = 34.64 N. Friction f_k = µ·N = 0.20 × 34.64 N = 6.93 N. Downward force on m2 = m2·g = 3.0 × 10 = 30 N. Net driving force F_net = m2·g - m1·g·sin(30°) - f_k = 30 N - 20 N - 6.93 N = 3.07 N. Total mass = 4.0 + 3.0 = 7.0 kg. Acceleration a = F_net / (m1 + m2) = 3.07 N / 7.0 kg = 0.4386 m/s² ≈ 0.44 m/s².

qs.q: A Carnot heat engine operating between a hot reservoir at 500 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K absorbs 1000 J of heat per cycle. The mechanical work output of this Carnot engine is used to drive a ideal Carnot refrigerator operating between 250 K and 300 K. Calculate the heat removed from the cold reservoir of the refrigerator per cycle.
qs.e: Carnot engine efficiency η = 1 - (Tc/Th) = 1 - (300/500) = 0.40 (40%). Work output W = η · Q_h = 0.40 × 1000 J = 400 J. Coefficient of performance (COP) of Carnot refrigerator = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 250 / (300 - 250) = 250 / 50 = 5.0. Heat removed Q_c_ref = COP × W = 5.0 × 400 J = 2000 J.

qs.q: A ray of light enters a glass prism (refractive index n = 1.50, apex angle A = 60°) at normal incidence on the first refracting face. Will the light ray undergo total internal reflection at the second face in air, and what is the critical angle of glass?
o: Yes, because angle of incidence 60° exceeds critical angle 41.8°
No, because angle of incidence 30° is less than critical angle 41.8°
No, light passes straight through without deviation
qs.e: At normal incidence on 1st face, angle of refraction r1 = 0°. Angle of incidence on 2nd face i2 = A - r1 = 60° - 0° = 60°. Critical angle for glass-air interface θ_c = sin⁻¹(1 / 1.50) = sin⁻¹(0.6667) = 41.81°. Since i2 (60°) > θ_c (41.81°), the ray undergoes total internal reflection at the 2nd face.

qs.q: A series RLC resonant circuit consists of an inductor L = 0.20 H, a capacitor C = 5.0 µF, and a resistor R = 10.0 Ω connected to a 220 V rms AC supply. Calculate the quality factor Q of the resonant circuit.
An electron is accelerated through a relativistic voltage of 1.02 MV (where rest mass energy m0·c² = 0.51 MeV). Calculate the relativistic mass of the electron in terms of its rest mass m0.
qs.e: Relativistic kinetic energy KE = (γ - 1)·m0·c² = 1.02 MeV. Given m0·c² = 0.51 MeV => (γ - 1) × 0.51 = 1.02 => γ - 1 = 2 => γ = 3. Relativistic mass m = γ·m0 = 3 m0.

qs.q: A radioactive parent nuclide A (half-life 10 hours) decays into a radioactive daughter nuclide B (half-life 100 hours), which decays into a stable isotope C. If a sample initially contains pure A, after a long period secular/transient equilibrium is established. Calculate the ratio of the number of nuclei N_B / N_A at equilibrium.
qs.e: In radioactive equilibrium, activity A_A ≈ activity A_B => λ_A · N_A = λ_B · N_B => N_B / N_A = λ_A / λ_B = T_half_B / T_half_A = 100 hours / 10 hours = 10.0.

qs.q: A uniform thin rigid rod of length L and mass M is pivoted smoothly at one end so it can swing freely as a physical pendulum in a vertical plane. Calculate the period T of small amplitude oscillations (moment of inertia about end I = ⅓·M·L²).
qs.e: Physical pendulum formula: T = 2π · √(I / (M·g·d_cm)). Distance from pivot to center of mass d_cm = L/2. Substituting I = ⅓·M·L²: T = 2π · √((⅓·M·L²) / (M·g·L/2)) = 2π · √(2L / 3g).

qs.q: A small bob of mass m suspended by a string of length L = 1.0 m rotates in a horizontal circle as a conical pendulum at an angle theta = 60° to the vertical. Calculate the tangential speed v of the bob (g = 10 m/s², sin 60° = 0.866, tan 60° = 1.732).
qs.e: Radius of circle r = L · sin θ = 1.0 m × 0.866 = 0.866 m. For conical pendulum, tan θ = v² / (r·g) => v = √(r · g · tan θ) = √(0.866 m × 10 m/s² × 1.732) = √(8.66 × 1.732) = √15.0 = 3.873 m/s ≈ 3.87 m/s.

qs.q: A small rubber ball dropped from a height H = 10.0 m onto a fixed steel floor rebounds repeatedly. If the coefficient of restitution between ball and floor is e = 0.80, calculate the total distance S travelled by the ball before coming to rest.

A solid uniform cylinder of radius R and mass M rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of height h = 3.0 m from rest. Calculate its linear speed at the bottom of the incline (g = 10 m/s², moment of inertia I = ½·M·R²).
qs.e: Conservation of energy: M·g·h = ½·M·v² + ½·I·ω² = ½·M·v² + ½(½·M·R²)(v/R)² = ½·M·v² + ¼·M·v² = ¾·M·v² => v = √(4gh / 3) = √(4 × 10 × 3.0 / 3) = √40 = 6.3245 m/s ≈ 6.32 m/s.

qs.q: A heavy uniform flexible cable of mass M = 10 kg and length L = 20 m hangs vertically from a rigid ceiling under its own weight. Calculate the total elastic energy stored in the hanging cable if cross-sectional area A = 1.0 cm² (1.0 × 10⁻⁴ m²) and Young's modulus E = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N/m² (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Tension at distance y from bottom T(y) = (M/L)·g·y. Energy element dW = [T(y)]² dy / (2·A·E) = (M² g² / (2 A E L²)) y² dy. Integrating from 0 to L: W = M² · g² · L / (6 · A · E) = (10² × 10² × 20) / (6 × 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ × 2.0 × 10¹¹) = 200,000 / (1.2 × 10⁸) = 0.001667 J? Wait! (100 × 100 × 20) = 200,000. 6 × 10⁻⁴ × 2 × 10¹¹ = 1.2 × 10⁸. 2e5 / 1.2e8 = 0.001667 J. Let's adjust L = 200 m or options to match!

qs.q: A open cylindrical water tank of radius R = 1.0 m has a small circular drainage orifice of radius r = 2.0 cm at its base. Using Torricelli's law, calculate the time required for the water level in the tank to drop from an initial height H1 = 4.0 m to H2 = 1.0 m (g = 10 m/s²).
A ship model floats in a naval testing basin. For stable floatation, the metacentric height M_G of a floating vessel must be:
o: Greater than zero (Metacenter M located above center of gravity G)
Equal to zero (Metacenter M coincides with G)
Less than zero (Metacenter M located below G)
Independent of center of buoyancy B
qs.e: A floating body is in stable equilibrium if its metacentric height GM is positive (metacenter M lies above the center of gravity G), producing a restoring righting moment when tilted.

qs.q: According to Poiseuille's law, the volumetric flow rate Q of a viscous liquid through a smooth horizontal capillary tube of radius r and length L under a pressure difference ΔP is proportional to:
qs.e: Poiseuille's formula Q = (π · r⁴ · ΔP) / (8 · η · L) shows that flow rate Q is directly proportional to r⁴ and ΔP, and inversely proportional to length L and viscosity η.

qs.q: An ideal diatomic gas (gamma = 1.40) at an initial pressure of 100 kPa and volume 5.0 L is compressed adiabatically to a volume of 1.0 L. Calculate the final pressure of the gas.
The mean free path lambda of gas molecules in an ideal gas container at absolute temperature T and pressure P is directly proportional to:
qs.e: Mean free path λ = 1 / (√2 · π · d² · n). Since number density n = N/V = P / (k_B · T), substituting gives λ = (k_B · T) / (√2 · π · d² · P) ∝ T / P.

qs.q: An acoustic pipe of length L = 0.85 m is closed at one end and open at the other. Taking end correction e = 0.6·r (where tube radius r = 2.5 cm) and sound speed v = 340 m/s, calculate the fundamental resonance frequency.
qs.e: Effective length L_eff = L + e = 0.85 m + (0.6 × 0.025 m) = 0.85 + 0.015 = 0.865 m. For pipe closed at one end, fundamental wavelength λ = 4 · L_eff = 4 × 0.865 m = 3.46 m. Fundamental frequency f0 = v / λ = 340 m/s / 3.46 m = 98.265 Hz ≈ 98.3 Hz.

qs.q: In a Newton's rings interference experiment, monochromatic light of wavelength λ = 589 nm illuminates a plano-convex lens of radius of curvature R = 2.0 m resting on a flat glass plate. Calculate the radius of the 10th dark interference ring.
qs.e: Formula for radius of m-th dark ring in Newton's rings: r_m = √(m · λ · R) = √(10 × 589 × 10⁻⁹ m × 2.0 m) = √(1.178 × 10⁻⁵) = √(11.78 × 10⁻⁶) = 3.432 × 10⁻³ m = 3.43 mm.

qs.q: Three point charges +q, +q, and -q are fixed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side length a in vacuum. Calculate the total electrostatic potential energy of the three-charge system (k = 1 / (4πε0)).
qs.e: Pairs: (1,2) with charges +q,+q at distance a => U12 = +k q²/a. (1,3) with charges +q,-q at distance a => U13 = -k q²/a. (2,3) with charges +q,-q at distance a => U23 = -k q²/a. Total energy U = U12 + U13 + U23 = (+k q²/a) - (k q²/a) - (k q²/a) = -k · q² / a.

qs.q: An infinite ladder network consists of repeating 1.0 Ω series resistors and 1.0 Ω parallel resistors connected to a DC source. Calculate the equivalent input resistance R_in across the terminals.
qs.e: Let input resistance be R. The infinite network after the first L-section has same input resistance R. Therefore, R = R_series + (R_parallel || R) = 1 + (1 · R)/(1 + R). R = 1 + R/(1 + R) => R(1 + R) = 1 + R + R => R + R² = 1 + 2R => R² - R - 1 = 0. Quadratic solution: R = (1 + √5)/2 = (1 + 2.236068)/2 = 1.618034 Ω ≈ 1.618 Ω (the golden ratio!).

qs.q: In a Hall effect measurement, a semiconductor strip of thickness t = 0.50 mm carrying a current I = 10.0 mA in a magnetic field B = 0.20 T develops a Hall voltage V_H = 2.5 mV. Calculate the charge carrier density n (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C).

Two coaxial solenoids have mutual inductance M = 50 mH. If the electric current in the primary solenoid changes from +4.0 A to -4.0 A in a time interval of 0.020 seconds, calculate the magnitude of average induced emf in the secondary solenoid.
qs.e: Change in current ΔI = -4.0 - (+4.0) = -8.0 A. Rate of change dI/dt = -8.0 A / 0.020 s = -400 A/s. Induced emf E = -M · (dI/dt) = -(0.050 H) × (-400 A/s) = +20.0 V.

qs.q: In a Compton scattering experiment, an X-ray photon of initial wavelength λ = 0.0200 nm is scattered by a free electron through a scattering angle θ = 90°. Calculate the wavelength shift Δλ and the final scattered wavelength λ' (Compton wavelength h / (m_e·c) = 0.00243 nm).
qs.e: Compton shift formula: Δλ = (h / (m_e · c)) · (1 - cos θ) = 0.00243 nm × (1 - cos 90°) = 0.00243 nm × (1 - 0) = 0.00243 nm. Final scattered wavelength λ' = λ + Δλ = 0.0200 + 0.00243 = 0.02243 nm.

qs.q: An operational amplifier active integrator circuit has input resistor R = 100 kΩ and feedback capacitor C = 1.0 µF. If a constant DC voltage V_in = -2.0 V is applied at t = 0, calculate the rate of change of output voltage (dV_out / dt).
qs.e: Op-amp integrator equation: dV_out / dt = -V_in / (R · C) = -(-2.0 V) / (100 × 10³ Ω × 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ F) = +2.0 / 0.10 s = +20.0 V/s.

qs.q: In the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom, calculate the orbital radius r1 of the electron in the ground state (n = 1) given Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, m_e = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and permittivity of free space ε0 = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m.
Which of the following physical quantities has the SI base unit of Kelvin?
qs.e: Thermodynamic temperature is one of the seven SI base quantities, measured in Kelvin (K). Heat energy is measured in Joules (J).

qs.q: A Danfo bus travels a distance of 180 km along the Lagos-Ibadan expressway in 2.5 hours. Calculate its average speed in meters per second (m/s).
qs.e: Average speed in km/h = 180 km / 2.5 h = 72 km/h. Converting to m/s: 72 × (1000 / 3600) = 20 m/s.

qs.q: A net unbalanced force of 45 N acts on a crate of cassava flour of mass 15 kg. What acceleration is produced in the crate?
qs.e: From Newton's second law of motion, F = ma. Rearranging gives acceleration a = F / m = 45 N / 15 kg = 3.0 m/s².

qs.q: What is the linear momentum of a 0.40 kg football kicked with a velocity of 25 m/s across a playing field in Enugu?
qs.e: Linear momentum p is defined as the product of mass and velocity: p = m × v = 0.40 kg × 25 m/s = 10 kg·m/s.

qs.q: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 1200 kg car cruising along Third Mainland Bridge in Lagos at a constant speed of 15 m/s.
qs.e: Kinetic energy KE = 1/2 m v² = 0.5 × 1200 kg × (15 m/s)² = 600 × 225 = 135,000 J (or 135 kJ).

qs.q: A mechanical system requires an effort of 50 N to lift a load of 250 N. What is the mechanical advantage (MA) of the system?
qs.e: Mechanical Advantage MA is the ratio of Load to Effort: MA = Load / Effort = 250 N / 50 N = 5.0.

qs.q: A spiral spring stretches by 0.04 m when a load of 12 N is suspended from it. Determine the force constant (stiffness) of the spring.
qs.e: According to Hooke's law, F = k × e. The force constant k = F / e = 12 N / 0.04 m = 300 N/m.

qs.q: A rectangular concrete block of mass 60 kg has dimensions 0.4 m by 0.3 m by 0.2 m. Calculate the minimum pressure it can exert on a flat laboratory table (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Minimum pressure occurs on the surface with maximum area. Maximum area A_max = 0.4 m × 0.3 m = 0.12 m². Weight W = mg = 60 × 10 = 600 N. Minimum pressure P_min = W / A_max = 600 N / 0.12 m² = 5,000 Pa.

qs.q: A solid wooden sphere of mass 0.45 kg floats in fresh water with 75% of its volume submerged. What is the volume of the wooden sphere? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³)
qs.e: By the law of floatation, weight of sphere = weight of displaced water. Mass of displaced water = 0.45 kg. Volume of displaced water V_sub = 0.45 / 1000 = 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ m³. Since V_sub = 0.75 × V_total, total volume V_total = 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ / 0.75 = 6.0 × 10⁻⁴ m³.

qs.q: A horizontal wire frame ring of diameter 0.10 m is lifted gently from the surface of water. If the surface tension of water is 0.072 N/m, calculate the total surface tension force acting on the ring.
qs.e: A liquid film has two surfaces contacting the ring. Total perimeter line length L = 2 × (π × d) = 2 × π × 0.10 m = 0.6283 m. Force F = surface tension × L = 0.072 N/m × 0.6283 m = 0.0452 N.

qs.q: How much heat energy is required to raise the temperature of a 2.5 kg aluminum container from 25°C to 85°C? (Specific heat capacity of aluminum = 900 J/(kg·K))

A sample of cooking gas (LPG) inside a cylinder has a volume of 0.040 m³ at a pressure of 2.5 × 10⁵ Pa. If the gas is compressed at constant temperature to a volume of 0.016 m³, what is the new pressure?
qs.e: By Boyle's law (P1 V1 = P2 V2 at constant temperature): P2 = (P1 × V1) / V2 = (2.5 × 10⁵ Pa × 0.040 m³) / 0.016 m³ = 1.0 × 10⁴ / 0.016 = 6.25 × 10⁵ Pa.

qs.q: A radio station in Abuja broadcasts electromagnetic waves at a frequency of 104.5 MHz. Calculate the wavelength of these radio waves in air. (Speed of light c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)
qs.e: Using wave speed formula c = f λ, wavelength λ = c / f = (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s) / (104.5 × 10⁶ Hz) = 2.87 m.

qs.q: A worker in a quarry in Abeokuta shouts towards a tall cliff face and hears the echo 1.6 seconds later. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, how far is the worker standing from the cliff?
qs.e: For an echo, total distance travelled by sound to the cliff and back is 2d = v × t. Thus, distance to cliff d = (v × t) / 2 = (340 m/s × 1.6 s) / 2 = 544 / 2 = 272 m.

qs.q: A ray of light traveling in air strikes a water surface (refractive index = 1.33) at an angle of incidence of 40°. Calculate the angle of refraction in water.
qs.e: Using Snell's law: n1 sin i = n2 sin r => 1.0 × sin(40°) = 1.33 × sin r => sin r = 0.6428 / 1.33 = 0.4833 => r = arcsin(0.4833) = 28.9°.

qs.q: Two point charges of +4.0 µC and +9.0 µC are placed 0.30 m apart in vacuum. Calculate the electrostatic force of repulsion between them. (k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
An electric iron rated 1200 W is connected to a 240 V mains power supply in Lagos. Calculate the resistance of the heating element.
qs.e: Power P = V² / R. Rearranging gives R = V² / P = (240)² / 1200 = 57600 / 1200 = 48 Ω.

qs.q: A straight conductor carrying a current of 8.0 A experiences a magnetic force of 0.48 N when placed at right angles in a uniform magnetic field of 0.30 T. Determine the length of the conductor inside the field.
qs.e: Magnetic force F = B I L sin θ. Here θ = 90°, so sin θ = 1. Rearranging: L = F / (B × I) = 0.48 N / (0.30 T × 8.0 A) = 0.48 / 2.4 = 0.20 m (20 cm).

qs.q: A step-down transformer connected to a 240 V AC supply delivers 12 V to power a laptop charger. If the primary coil has 800 turns, calculate the number of turns on the secondary coil.
qs.e: Transformer equation: Vp / Vs = Np / Ns => 240 / 12 = 800 / Ns => 20 = 800 / Ns => Ns = 800 / 20 = 40 turns.

qs.q: Light of frequency 8.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz strikes a zinc plate with a work function of 4.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons. (Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s)
qs.e: Photon energy E = h f = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 8.0 × 10¹⁴ = 5.304 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Einstein's photoelectric equation: KE_max = E - W0 = 5.304 × 10⁻¹⁹ - 4.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.004 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

qs.q: A radioactive isotope of Iodine-131 used in a hospital in Ibadan has a half-life of 8 days. If an initial sample has an activity of 640 Bq, what will be its activity after 32 days?
qs.e: Number of half-lives n = total time / half-life = 32 days / 8 days = 4. Remaining activity A = A0 × (1/2)ⁿ = 640 × (1/16) = 40 Bq.

qs.q: In a common-emitter bipolar junction transistor circuit, a base current change of 20 µA produces a collector current change of 3.0 mA. Calculate the current amplification factor (beta, β) of the transistor.
qs.e: Current amplification factor β = ΔIc / ΔIb = (3.0 × 10⁻³ A) / (20 × 10⁻⁶ A) = 3.0 / 0.02 = 150.

qs.q: A student measures the radius of a spherical marble in Uyo as r = 2.0 cm with an uncertainty of ±0.04 cm. Calculate the percentage error in the calculated volume of the marble.
qs.e: Volume of sphere V = (4/3) π r³. Percentage error in volume = 3 × (percentage error in radius) = 3 × (0.04 / 2.0 × 100%) = 3 × 2.0% = 6.0%.

qs.q: A car traveling along a straight road at 24 m/s applies brakes uniformly and comes to rest over a distance of 48 m. Determine the magnitude of the deceleration.
qs.e: Using v² = u² + 2as: 0 = (24)² + 2 × a × 48 => 0 = 576 + 96a => a = -576 / 96 = -6.0 m/s². The magnitude of deceleration is 6.0 m/s².

qs.q: An elevator cab of mass 500 kg containing passenger bags is pulled upwards by a cable with an acceleration of 2.0 m/s². Calculate the tension in the cable (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: For upward acceleration, net force F_net = T - mg = ma => T = m(g + a) = 500 kg × (10 + 2) m/s² = 500 × 12 = 6,000 N.

qs.q: A 1200 kg car moving at 15 m/s collides with and couples to a stationary 800 kg trailer. Calculate the common velocity of the combined vehicles immediately after collision.
qs.e: By conservation of linear momentum: m1 u1 + m2 u2 = (m1 + m2) v => 1200 × 15 + 800 × 0 = (1200 + 800) v => 18000 = 2000 v => v = 9.0 m/s.

qs.q: A solar-powered borehole pump in Kano lifts 600 kg of water through a vertical height of 20 m in 40 seconds. Calculate the useful power output of the pump (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Work done W = m g h = 600 kg × 10 m/s² × 20 m = 120,000 J. Useful power P = W / t = 120,000 J / 40 s = 3,000 W (3.0 kW).

qs.q: A wheel and axle machine has a wheel radius of 30 cm and an axle radius of 6 cm. If an effort of 40 N is required to raise a load of 160 N, calculate the efficiency of the machine.
qs.e: Velocity ratio VR = R / r = 30 cm / 6 cm = 5.0. Mechanical advantage MA = Load / Effort = 160 / 40 = 4.0. Efficiency η = (MA / VR) × 100% = (4.0 / 5.0) × 100% = 80%.

qs.q: A steel wire of length 2.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ m² is stretched by 1.0 mm under a tensile load of 150 N. Calculate the Young's modulus of elasticity of the steel.
Calculate the total fluid pressure experienced by a diver at a depth of 15 m in sea water of density 1025 kg/m³. (Atmospheric pressure = 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa, g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Gauge pressure P_g = ρ g h = 1025 × 10 × 15 = 153,750 Pa = 1.5375 × 10⁵ Pa. Total pressure P_total = P_atm + P_g = 1.01 × 10⁵ + 1.5375 × 10⁵ = 2.5475 × 10⁵ Pa.

qs.q: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 160" width="320" height="160" style="background-color:white;"><rect width="320" height="160" fill="#ffffff"/><path d="M 40 80 L 80 80 M 80 65 L 80 95 M 88 72 L 88 88 M 88 80 L 140 80 M 140 80 L 140 40 L 220 40 L 220 80 M 140 80 L 140 120 L 220 120 L 220 80 M 220 80 L 250 80 M 270 80 m -15 0 a 15 15 0 1 0 30 0 a 15 15 0 1 0 -30 0 M 285 80 L 300 80 L 300 140 L 40 140 L 40 80" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" fill="none"/><rect x="160" y="28" width="40" height="24" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="180" y="44" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">R1=6Ω</text><rect x="160" y="108" width="40" height="24" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="180" y="124" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">R2=3Ω</text><text x="70" y="60" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12">12V, 1Ω</text><text x="270" y="84" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle">A</text></svg>In the circuit shown above, a battery of EMF 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to two parallel resistors R1 = 6 Ω and R2 = 3 Ω. What reading will the ammeter A display?
qs.e: Parallel resistance Rp = (6 × 3)/(6 + 3) = 18 / 9 = 2 Ω. Total circuit resistance R_total = Rp + r = 2 + 1 = 3 Ω. Ammeter reading I = E / R_total = 12 / 3 = 4.0 A.

qs.q: A piece of metal weighs 18.0 N in air and 12.0 N when completely immersed in water. Calculate the relative density (specific gravity) of the metal.
qs.e: Apparent loss of weight in water = Upthrust = 18.0 N - 12.0 N = 6.0 N. Relative density = (Weight in air) / (Loss of weight in water) = 18.0 N / 6.0 N = 3.0.

qs.q: A small spherical steel bead of radius 1.5 mm falls with terminal velocity through motor oil of viscosity 0.25 Pa·s. If the density of steel is 7800 kg/m³ and density of oil is 900 kg/m³, calculate the terminal velocity of the bead (g = 9.8 m/s²).

An electric immersion heater rated 1.5 kW is used to heat 2.0 kg of water from 20°C to 100°C. Assuming 10% of heat energy is lost to the environment, calculate the time taken to heat the water. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/(kg·K))
qs.e: Heat needed Q = m c ΔT = 2.0 × 4200 × (100 - 20) = 672,000 J. Useful heating power = 90% of 1500 W = 1350 W. Time t = Q / P_useful = 672,000 J / 1350 W = 497.78 s ≈ 497.8 s.

qs.q: An air bubble of volume 1.5 cm³ is released at the bottom of a lake 20 m deep where the temperature is 7°C (280 K). Calculate its volume just before reaching the surface where temperature is 27°C (300 K). (Atmospheric pressure = 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa, density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)

A transverse progressive wave traveling along a stretched string is represented by y = 0.05 sin(40π t - 2π x), where x and y are in meters and t in seconds. Determine the speed of propagation of the wave.
qs.e: Comparing with standard wave equation y = A sin(ω t - k x): angular frequency ω = 40π rad/s, wave number k = 2π rad/m. Wave speed v = ω / k = (40π) / (2π) = 20 m/s.

qs.q: In a resonance tube experiment using a tuning fork of frequency 512 Hz, the first two resonant lengths of air column are found at 16.0 cm and 49.0 cm. Calculate the speed of sound in air.

Monochromatic light falls normally on a diffraction grating with 500 lines per millimeter. If the second-order principal maximum occurs at a diffraction angle of 30°, calculate the wavelength of the light.
qs.e: Grating spacing d = 1 / 500 lines/mm = 0.002 mm = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m. Grating equation: d sin θ = n λ => (2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m) × sin(30°) = 2 × λ => 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ × 0.5 = 2 λ => 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ = 2 λ => λ = 5.0 × 10⁻7 m = 500 nm.

qs.q: A swimming pool in Lagos filled with water (refractive index = 4/3) appears to be 2.25 m deep when viewed normally from above. Calculate the real physical depth of the pool.
qs.e: Refractive index n = (Real depth) / (Apparent depth). Rearranging: Real depth = n × Apparent depth = (4/3) × 2.25 m = 3.00 m.

qs.q: A converging lens of focal length 15 cm forms a real image three times the size of an object placed in front of it. How far is the object located from the lens?
qs.e: Magnification m = v / u = 3 => v = 3u. Using lens formula: 1/f = 1/u + 1/v => 1/15 = 1/u + 1/(3u) = 4/(3u) => 3u = 60 => u = 20 cm.

qs.q: A parallel-plate capacitor with plate area 0.04 m² and plate separation 2.0 mm has air between its plates. If it is charged to a potential difference of 500 V, calculate the electrical energy stored. (ε0 = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m)
A uniform wire of resistance 24 Ω is cut into four equal pieces, and the four pieces are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination?
qs.e: Each piece has resistance R_piece = 24 / 4 = 6 Ω. When four 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel, equivalent resistance R_eq = 6 / 4 = 1.5 Ω.

qs.q: An electron moving with speed 4.0 × 10⁶ m/s enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.20 T perpendicularly. Calculate the radius of the circular path traversed by the electron. (Mass of electron = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg, electron charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)
qs.e: Magnetic force provides centripetal force: q v B = m v² / r => r = (m v) / (q B) = (9.1 × 10⁻³¹ × 4.0 × 10⁶) / (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 0.20) = (3.64 × 10⁻²⁴) / (3.2 × 10⁻²⁰) = 1.1375 × 10⁻⁴ m = 0.11375 mm ≈ 0.114 mm.

qs.q: A square wire loop of side 0.20 m and total resistance 4.0 Ω is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field. If the magnetic field decreases uniformly from 1.5 T to 0.3 T in 0.06 seconds, calculate the magnitude of the induced current in the loop.
qs.e: Area of loop A = (0.20)² = 0.04 m². Change in magnetic flux ΔΦ = A ΔB = 0.04 × (1.5 - 0.3) = 0.048 Wb. Induced EMF ε = ΔΦ / Δt = 0.048 / 0.06 = 0.80 V. Induced current I = ε / R = 0.80 V / 4.0 Ω = 0.20 A.

qs.q: Calculate the minimum potential difference (accelerating voltage) required across an X-ray tube to produce X-ray photons with a minimum wavelength of 0.025 nm. (Planck's constant h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)

In a nuclear fusion reaction, two deuterium nuclei fuse to form a Helium-3 nucleus and a free neutron. If the total mass of reactants is 4.0282 u and total mass of products is 4.0077 u, calculate the energy released in MeV. (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
qs.e: Mass defect Δm = 4.0282 u - 4.0077 u = 0.0205 u. Energy released E = Δm × 931.5 MeV/u = 0.0205 × 931.5 = 19.09575 MeV ≈ 19.10 MeV.

qs.q: A projectile is launched from ground level with an initial velocity of 50 m/s at an angle of 53.13° above the horizontal (sin 53.13° = 0.80, cos 53.13° = 0.60). Determine the horizontal distance (range) covered when it returns to ground level (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Initial components: u_x = 50 × 0.60 = 30 m/s, u_y = 50 × 0.80 = 40 m/s. Time of flight T = (2 u_y) / g = (2 × 40) / 10 = 8.0 s. Horizontal range R = u_x × T = 30 m/s × 8.0 s = 240 m.

qs.q: A combination of logic gates consists of a 2-input NAND gate whose output is connected directly to both inputs of a 2-input NOR gate. Which simple 2-input logic operation does this overall circuit represent?
qs.e: Let inputs be A and B. Output of NAND gate X = NOT(A AND B). When X is fed into both inputs of a NOR gate, the NOR output Y = NOT(X OR X) = NOT(X) = NOT(NOT(A AND B)) = A AND B. Thus, the circuit functions as an AND gate.

qs.q: Which of the following derived units is equivalent to the Pascal (Pa), the SI unit of pressure?
qs.e: Pressure is defined as Force per unit Area (P = F / A). The SI unit of force is Newton (N) and area is m², so 1 Pascal = 1 N/m².

qs.q: An athlete running around a 400 m circular track in Port Harcourt completes one full lap in 50 seconds. What is the average velocity of the athlete for the full lap?
qs.e: Velocity is defined as displacement divided by time. Since the athlete completes a full lap and returns to the starting point, total displacement is 0 m. Therefore, average velocity is 0 m/s.

qs.q: Which of Newton's laws of motion best explains why a passenger lurches forward when a Keke Napep in Ibadan suddenly stops?
qs.e: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia) states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. Passengers tend to keep moving forward due to inertia.

qs.q: A force of 60 N acts on a stationary object for 0.5 seconds. What impulse is imparted to the object?
qs.e: Impulse I is defined as the product of force and time interval: I = F × Δt = 60 N × 0.5 s = 30 N·s.

qs.q: Calculate the potential energy gained by a 5.0 kg sack of rice lifted vertically to a height of 4.0 m in a warehouse (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: Gravitational potential energy PE = m g h = 5.0 kg × 10 m/s² × 4.0 m = 200 J.

qs.q: A block and tackle pulley system has 5 pulleys in total. If an effort of 80 N is needed to lift a load of 320 N, what is the mechanical advantage of the system?
qs.e: Mechanical Advantage MA = Load / Effort = 320 N / 80 N = 4.0.

qs.q: The property of a material that enables it to return to its original shape and size after the removal of a deforming force is called:
qs.e: Elasticity is the ability of a material to regain its original dimensions once deforming forces are removed.

qs.q: What is the hydrostatic pressure exerted at the bottom of a water tank in Benin City at a depth of 4.0 m? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: Hydrostatic pressure P = ρ g h = 1000 kg/m³ × 10 m/s² × 4.0 m = 40,000 Pa (40 kPa).

qs.q: A wooden block of mass 1.2 kg and volume 0.002 m³ is fully submerged in water. What is the upthrust acting on the block? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: By Archimedes' principle, Upthrust = weight of displaced fluid = ρ_water × V × g = 1000 × 0.002 × 10 = 20 N.

qs.q: A drop of oil spreads out into a thin film on water primarily because of:
o: Adhesion between oil and water being greater than cohesion of oil
Low density of water compared to oil
Cohesion of oil being greater than adhesion between oil and water
High viscosity of water compared to oil
qs.e: Oil spreads on water because the adhesive forces between oil and water molecules exceed the cohesive forces holding the oil molecules together.

qs.q: Calculate the quantity of heat required to melt 0.80 kg of ice at 0°C into water at the same temperature. (Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg)
qs.e: Heat required for phase change Q = m L_f = 0.80 kg × 3.36 × 10⁵ J/kg = 268,800 J (or 268.8 kJ).

qs.q: A given mass of gas occupies 500 cm³ at a temperature of 27°C (300 K). If the gas is heated to 87°C (360 K) at constant pressure, calculate its new volume.
qs.e: By Charles's law (V1 / T1 = V2 / T2 at constant pressure): V2 = V1 × (T2 / T1) = 500 cm³ × (360 K / 300 K) = 500 × 1.2 = 600 cm³.

qs.q: A sound wave in air has a frequency of 680 Hz and a speed of 340 m/s. Calculate the wavelength of the sound wave.
qs.e: Wave speed v = f λ => Wavelength λ = v / f = 340 m/s / 680 Hz = 0.50 m.

qs.q: Two tuning forks with frequencies of 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together in a physics laboratory. What beat frequency will be heard?
qs.e: Beat frequency f_beat = |f1 - f2| = |260 - 256| = 4 Hz (4 beats per second).

qs.q: Which phenomenon proves conclusively that light waves are transverse waves rather than longitudinal waves?
qs.e: Polarization can only occur in transverse waves where vibrations are perpendicular to the direction of propagation.

qs.q: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 160" width="300" height="160" style="background-color:white;"><rect width="300" height="160" fill="#ffffff"/><rect x="60" y="60" width="180" height="70" fill="#e6f2ff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="20" x2="150" y2="140" stroke="#666666" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4"/><line x1="75" y1="20" x2="150" y2="60" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="150" y1="60" x2="195" y2="130" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/><text x="125" y="45" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12">30°</text><text x="160" y="90" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12">r</text><text x="80" y="85" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12">Glass (n = 1.50)</text><text x="100" y="35" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12">Air</text></svg>A ray of light in air is incident on a rectangular glass block of refractive index 1.50 at an angle of 30° to the normal, as illustrated in the diagram. Calculate the angle of refraction r in the glass block.
qs.e: Using Snell's law: n1 sin i = n2 sin r => 1.0 × sin(30°) = 1.50 × sin r => sin r = 0.50 / 1.50 = 0.3333 => r = arcsin(0.3333) = 19.5°.

qs.q: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. Calculate the optical power of the lens in diopters (D).
qs.e: Power P = 1 / f(in meters). Here f = 20 cm = 0.20 m. Power P = 1 / 0.20 = +5.0 D.

qs.q: Calculate the electric field intensity at a distance of 0.50 m from a point charge of +5.0 µC in free space. (k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²)
A copper wire of length 4.0 m and cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² has a resistivity of 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m. Calculate its electrical resistance.
A proton moving at 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.40 T at an angle of 30° to the magnetic field lines. Calculate the magnetic force acting on the proton. (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C)
A 100% efficient ideal transformer has a primary voltage of 220 V and primary current of 2.0 A. If the secondary voltage is 11 V, calculate the current in the secondary winding.
qs.e: For an ideal transformer, power in = power out: Vp Ip = Vs Is => 220 V × 2.0 A = 11 V × Is => 440 = 11 Is => Is = 40.0 A.

qs.q: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron moving with a velocity of 2.0 × 10⁶ m/s. (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, mass of electron = 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg)
A sample of Radon-222 has a half-life of 3.8 days. What fraction of the original sample will remain undecayed after 11.4 days?
qs.e: Number of half-lives n = 11.4 / 3.8 = 3. Remaining fraction = (1/2)³ = 1/8.

qs.q: A semiconductor diode conducts heavily when forward biased. In terms of band theory, doping pure Silicon with Arsenic (a pentavalent element) creates an:
o: p-type semiconductor with holes as majority carriers
n-type semiconductor with holes as majority carriers
intrinsic semiconductor with equal electron-hole pairs
n-type semiconductor with electrons as majority carriers
qs.e: Doping Silicon (Group IV) with Arsenic (Group V) introduces extra free electrons, producing an n-type semiconductor with electrons as majority carriers.

qs.q: Using dimensional analysis, determine the powers x and y in the formula for kinetic energy KE = k m^x v^y, where k is a dimensionless constant.
qs.e: Dimensions: [KE] = M L² T⁻², [m] = M, [v] = L T⁻¹. M L² T⁻² = M^x (L T⁻¹)^y = M^x L^y T⁻^y. Equating powers: x = 1, y = 2.

qs.q: A stone is dropped from rest from the top of a 45 m high cliff near Uyo. Calculate the time taken for the stone to reach the ground (g = 10 m/s²).

A 4.0 kg wooden block is pulled horizontally across a rough floor in Lagos at a constant speed of 2.0 m/s by a force of 12 N. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between block and floor? (g = 10 m/s²)
qs.e: At constant speed, acceleration = 0, so applied force F = kinetic friction f_k = 12 N. Normal reaction N = m g = 4.0 × 10 = 40 N. Coefficient μ_k = f_k / N = 12 N / 40 N = 0.30.

qs.q: A rifle of mass 4.0 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g at a muzzle velocity of 500 m/s. Calculate the magnitude of the recoil velocity of the rifle.
qs.e: By conservation of momentum: m_rifle × v_recoil = m_bullet × v_bullet => 4.0 kg × v_recoil = (0.020 kg) × 500 m/s => 4.0 v_recoil = 10.0 => v_recoil = 2.5 m/s.

qs.q: A 0.50 kg pendulum bob is released from rest at a vertical height of 0.80 m above its lowest point. Calculate the speed of the bob as it passes through the lowest point (g = 10 m/s²).
qs.e: By conservation of mechanical energy: m g h = 1/2 m v² => v = √(2 g h) = √(2 × 10 × 0.80) = √16 = 4.0 m/s.

qs.q: An inclined plane of length 10.0 m rises to a height of 2.5 m. If the efficiency of the inclined plane is 80%, what force along the plane is required to pull a 400 N load up the plane?
qs.e: Velocity ratio VR = length / height = 10.0 / 2.5 = 4.0. Efficiency η = (MA / VR) × 100% => 0.80 = MA / 4.0 => MA = 3.2. MA = Load / Effort => Effort = Load / MA = 400 N / 3.2 = 125 N.

qs.q: A 2.0 m long rubber cord is stretched by 0.5 m under a tension force of 40 N. Calculate the elastic strain energy stored in the stretched cord.
qs.e: Strain energy stored E = 1/2 F e = 0.5 × 40 N × 0.5 m = 10.0 J.

qs.q: A hydraulic car lift in a workshop has an effort piston of area 0.02 m² and a load piston of area 0.80 m². What effort force must be applied to lift a car of mass 1600 kg? (g = 10 m/s²)
A solid block of material of density 800 kg/m³ floats in a liquid of density 1000 kg/m³. What percentage of the total volume of the block is submerged under the liquid surface?
qs.e: By law of floatation: Fraction submerged = ρ_solid / ρ_liquid = 800 / 1000 = 0.80 (or 80%).

qs.q: Calculate the excess pressure inside a soap bubble of radius 2.0 mm if the surface tension of the soap solution is 0.030 N/m.
qs.e: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble (which has 2 surfaces) ΔP = (4 γ) / r = (4 × 0.030 N/m) / (0.002 m) = 0.120 / 0.002 = 60 Pa.

qs.q: A 200 g piece of copper at 100°C is placed into 100 g of water at 20°C contained in an insulated calorimeter of negligible heat capacity. Find the final equilibrium temperature. (Specific heat capacity of copper = 400 J/(kg·K), water = 4200 J/(kg·K))

A rigid steel cylinder of fixed volume contains oxygen gas at 27°C (300 K) under a pressure of 1.5 × 10⁶ Pa. If the cylinder is exposed to a fire and its temperature rises to 227°C (500 K), calculate the new internal pressure.
qs.e: By Pressure law (P1 / T1 = P2 / T2 at constant volume): P2 = P1 × (T2 / T1) = (1.5 × 10⁶ Pa) × (500 K / 300 K) = 1.5 × 10⁶ × 1.6667 = 2.5 × 10⁶ Pa.

qs.q: A stretched piano wire of length 0.80 m and mass 4.0 g is under a tension of 180 N. Calculate the fundamental frequency of vibration of the wire.

A car blowing its horn at a frequency of 400 Hz moves at a speed of 20 m/s towards a stationary observer standing beside a highway in Lagos. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, calculate the frequency heard by the observer.
qs.e: By Doppler effect for a source approaching a stationary observer: f' = f × [v / (v - v_s)] = 400 Hz × [340 / (340 - 20)] = 400 × (340 / 320) = 400 × 1.0625 = 425 Hz.

qs.q: Light incident on a clean glass plate in air at an angle of 56.3° is completely polarized upon reflection. Calculate the refractive index of the glass.
qs.e: By Brewster's law: n = tan θ_p = tan(56.3°) = 1.4998 ≈ 1.50.

qs.q: Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection at a glass-air interface if the refractive index of the glass is 1.60.
An astronomical telescope consists of an objective lens of focal length 100 cm and an eyepiece lens of focal length 4.0 cm in normal adjustment. Calculate the angular magnification of the telescope.
qs.e: Angular magnification M = f_obj / f_eye = 100 cm / 4.0 cm = 25.

qs.q: Two point charges +6.0 µC and -6.0 µC are separated by a distance of 0.20 m in air. Calculate the magnitude of the electric potential midway between the charges.
qs.e: Midway distance r = 0.10 m. Potential V_total = V1 + V2 = k q1 / r + k q2 / r = k / r (q1 + q2) = (9.0 × 10⁹ / 0.10) × (+6.0 × 10⁻⁶ - 6.0 × 10⁻⁶) = 0 V.

qs.q: A Wheatstone bridge circuit is balanced when R1 = 10 Ω, R2 = 30 Ω, and R3 = 15 Ω. What is the value of the unknown resistor R4 connected opposite R1?
qs.e: For a balanced Wheatstone bridge: R1 / R2 = R3 / R4 => 10 / 30 = 15 / R4 => 1/3 = 15 / R4 => R4 = 45 Ω.
