qs.e: Acts 7:60 records Stephen's Christlike spirit of forgiveness as the first Christian martyr: 'Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.'

qs.q: Saul's dramatic conversion occurred while he was traveling on the road to Damascus in order to
o: arrest Christians and bring them bound to Jerusalem
trade velvet goods with Syrian merchants
study law under foreign Greek philosophers
escape persecution from the High Priest
qs.e: Acts 9:1-2 explains Saul's objective: seeking letters from the High Priest to Damascus synagogues to imprison followers of 'the Way'.

qs.q: When the risen Lord appeared to Saul in a blinding light on the road to Damascus, the voice asked:
o: 'Saul, Saul, where is thy brother Stephen?'
'Saul, Saul, why breakest thou the Sabbath day?'
'Saul, Saul, why tarriest thou in Jerusalem?'
qs.e: Acts 9:4 records Jesus' words identifying Himself with His persecuted Church: 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?'

qs.q: In Romans 3:23-24, Paul states the universal human condition and solution by declaring that
o: human good works are sufficient to cancel personal guilt before God
salvation is achieved through strict compliance with ceremonial rituals
only Gentiles have sinned, while Jews are justified by Mosaic circumcision
for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; being justified freely by his grace
qs.e: Romans 3:23-24 establishes universal human sinfulness and free justification through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.

qs.q: In Ephesians 2:8-9, Paul clearly explains that believers are saved by
o: belonging to the physical lineage of Abraham
keeping the Ten Commandments and offering animal sacrifices
performing public penance before church elders
grace through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast
qs.e: Ephesians 2:8-9 encapsulates core salvation doctrine: unmerited grace received through faith alone, ruling out human boasting.

qs.q: The theological significance of human beings created in the 'image of God' (Imago Dei) in Genesis 1:26-27 is that
o: human mortality was rendered impossible prior to physical work
every human person possesses intrinsic dignity, moral capacity, and spiritual worth
humans share physical shape and material dimensions with the Divine Being
only kings and rulers carry divine authority over common people
qs.e: The Imago Dei in Genesis 1:26-27 establishes that humanity uniquely reflects God's moral, rational, and relational character, conferring sacred value and dignity upon every human life.

qs.q: The sacrifice of Isaac on Mount Moriah serves as a major typological shadow in biblical theology because it illustrates
o: the military conquest of Jerusalem by Abraham's descendants
a father's willing surrender of his beloved son and God's provision of a substitutionary sacrifice
that human obedience is optional when divine commands seem difficult
the absolute necessity of child sacrifice in ancient Near Eastern worship
qs.e: Genesis 22 illustrates substitutionary atonement ('God will provide himself a lamb') and foreshadows God offering His own Son, Isaac being a type of Christ.

qs.q: The overarching theological narrative of Joseph's life in Genesis 37-50 demonstrates that true forgiveness requires
o: exiling the offenders from the community permanently
pretending that past betrayals and sinful actions never occurred
demanding full financial compensation before offering emotional reconciliation
recognizing God's sovereign hand in adversity and releasing personal vengeance toward offenders
qs.e: Joseph's reconciliation with his brothers reveals that biblical forgiveness sees God's sovereign purpose behind suffering, replacing bitterness with mercy and practical care.

qs.q: In Old Testament theology, the Exodus event stands as the foundational historical benchmark of
o: the superiority of nomadic life over agricultural settlements
the permanent end of all sacrificial rituals
divine redemption and covenant nationhood for Israel
monarchical government established through military conquest
qs.e: The Exodus is Israel's central redemptive narrative, defining Yahweh as Redeemer and establishing Israel as His holy covenant nation (Exodus 19:5-6).

qs.q: The narrative of Samson demonstrates that personal charism and spiritual gifts without moral self-discipline and holiness lead to
o: personal compromise, spiritual blindness, and tragic self-destruction
immediate appointment as High Priest over the tabernacle
permanent freedom from temptation and moral failure
unbroken national prosperity and political stability
qs.e: Samson possessed immense physical strength gifted by the Spirit, but his lack of moral boundary and compromise with Delilah led to his blindness, captivity, and demise (Judges 16).

qs.q: The fundamental theological critique of Saul's reign compared to David's reign in Israelite history is that Saul
o: refused to build a permanent royal palace in Jerusalem
governed by human fear and self-preservation rather than wholehearted submission to Yahweh
was born from the tribe of Benjamin rather than Judah
lacked military courage on the battlefield against the Philistines
qs.e: Saul continually compromised God's word out of fear of men (1 Sam 15:24), while David, despite personal sins, was 'a man after God's own heart' who always sought Yahweh in true repentance.

qs.q: The spiritual failure of the northern kingdom of Israel compared to Judah was primarily caused by the fact that
o: Israel never had a single righteous king who eradicated state idolatry, leading inevitably to divine judgment
Israel lacked fertile land and experienced constant natural droughts
Judah possessed superior iron weaponry and walled fortifications
the Levites permanently abandoned all religious ministry in Canaan
qs.e: Every single northern king persisted in 'the sin of Jeroboam', producing an unbroken line of apostasy that led to Assyrian captivity in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:21-23).

qs.q: Comparing the ministries of Elijah and Elisha reveals that while Elijah's prophetic work was characterized by bold public confrontation with royal idolatry, Elisha's ministry focused extensively on
o: rebuilding the physical walls and gates of Jerusalem
widespread miraculous pastoral care, healing, and national counsel across diverse social strata
writing detailed apocalyptic prophecies regarding foreign empires
establishing an earthly kingdom centered in Damascus
qs.e: Elijah operated primarily as a fiery reformer confronting Ahab/Jezebel, while Elisha spent decades performing miracles of mercy, helping commoners, and advising kings.

qs.q: The primary theological lesson derived from Israel's Babylonian exile and subsequent restoration is that God's covenant relationship
o: involves righteous discipline for persistent sin, yet guarantees merciful restoration according to His divine promise
is permanently terminated whenever a nation experiences military defeat
applies exclusively to physical buildings and earthly geographic borders
guarantees physical invincibility regardless of moral unfaithfulness
qs.e: The exile vindicated God's holiness by punishing idolatry, while the restoration demonstrated His unwavering covenant faithfulness and mercy (Jeremiah 29:10-14).

qs.q: Comparing Proverbs, Job, and Ecclesiastes reveals that biblical wisdom literature as a whole teaches that
o: God rewards righteousness exclusively with financial wealth and physical health on earth
human wisdom is sufficient to solve every moral and cosmic dilemma independently
while standard moral cause-and-effect rules generally apply, ultimate trust belongs to God in life's mysteries and suffering
there is no moral judgment after physical death
qs.e: Proverbs provides general principles for wise living, while Job and Ecclesiastes address exceptions and mysteries, collectively directing humanity to reverent fear and trust in God.

qs.q: The primary theological distinction between pre-exilic major prophetic proclamations and exilic prophetic messages is that pre-exilic prophets focused on
o: advocating political treaties with Egypt and Assyria
instituting new sacrificial calendar feasts for the Temple
warning of imminent covenant judgment for idolatry, whereas exilic prophets offered hope and restoration
praising Israel's moral purity while condemning foreign Gentile nations
qs.e: Pre-exilic prophets (like early Isaiah and Jeremiah) confronted rampant sin with warnings of impending judgment, whereas exilic prophets (like Ezekiel and later Isaiah) comforted the broken exiles with promises of return and renewal.

qs.q: Malachi concludes the Old Testament canon (Malachi 4:5-6) with a messianic prophecy foretelling that before the great and dreadful day of the LORD, God will send
o: Moses the lawgiver to re-establish the tabernacle sacrifices
Elijah the prophet to turn the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers
Joshua the son of Nun to conquer the Gentile nations
King David to restore the earthly throne in Jerusalem
qs.e: Malachi 4:5-6 promises the coming of 'Elijah the prophet', fulfilled in John the Baptist who came in the spirit and power of Elijah to prepare Messiah's way (Luke 1:17, Matt 11:14).

qs.q: Theological reflection on the Virgin Birth (Incarnation) asserts that Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit so that He would be
o: an exalted angelic spirit appearing in a temporary human phantom body
a human prophet who attained divine status through flawless moral effort
a political monarch endowed with supernatural physical strength
fully God and fully human, unblemished by inherited sinful human nature
qs.e: The Incarnation (Luke 1:35) affirms that Jesus is truly God and truly man, holy and free from original sin, making Him the qualified mediator between God and humanity.

qs.q: The overarching contrast between the righteousness taught by Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount and that of the Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 5:20) is that Kingdom righteousness
o: permits personal retaliation provided it remains equal in severity
requires strict physical isolation from all Gentile taxpayers
is an internal heart reality produced by divine grace, exceeding outward, superficial legalism
depends entirely on physical descent from Abraham
qs.e: In Matthew 5:20, Jesus insists 'except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven,' demanding inner heart purity.

qs.q: Jesus' primary theological purpose for using parables in His teaching ministry (Matthew 13:10-15, Mark 4:11-12) was to
o: entertain large crowds with interesting fictional folk stories
replace the written Old Testament Scriptures with allegorical poetry
avoid paying taxes to the local Roman government officials
reveal spiritual truth to receptive, open hearts while concealing it from hardened, proud opponents
qs.e: Matthew 13:11-13 explains that parables unveil kingdom mysteries to disciples seeking truth while hiding them from those who deliberately reject God's word.

qs.q: In Gospel theology, the miracles of Jesus ('signs and wonders') served primarily as
o: attesting signs validating His messianic identity and demonstrating the present power of God's Kingdom
temporary natural phenomena unrelated to spiritual salvation
public magic shows to compel military rebellion against Rome
commercial ventures to generate revenue for the apostolic band
qs.e: John 20:30-31 states that Jesus' miraculous signs were recorded so that readers might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in His name.

qs.q: In Christian doctrine, the Resurrection of Jesus Christ is the absolute cornerstone of faith because, as Paul argues in 1 Corinthians 15, if Christ be not raised
o: the Church should convert into a political organization
the Mosaic Law remains in full ceremonial force over all Gentiles
our preaching is vain, your faith is also vain, and believers are yet in their sins
the Old Testament prophecies are proven to be human fables
qs.e: 1 Corinthians 15:14-17 asserts that Christ's bodily resurrection validates atonement; without it, faith is futile and humanity remains under condemnation.

qs.q: The appointment of the Seven in Acts 6 establishes an important leadership principle in the Church that
o: spiritual leadership requires delegating practical administrative duties to qualified believers to preserve focus on prayer and teaching
monetary giving is unnecessary in a Spirit-filled community
the pastoral ministry should handle all physical welfare duties personally
apostles possess absolute dictatorial rule without community input
qs.e: Acts 6:2-4 shows apostles refusing to neglect the Word of God for tables, establishing complementary roles where deacons handle administration and elders focus on prayer and ministry of the word.

qs.q: Peter's defense before the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:7-11) asserted that both Jews and Gentiles are saved
o: by combining Mosaic lawkeeping with faith in Christ
through separate covenant arrangements established by Moses and Paul
through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ in the exact same manner, by faith
by paying temple tithes in Jerusalem
qs.e: Acts 15:11 records Peter's definitive statement: 'We believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they,' establishing salvation by grace alone.

qs.q: Stephen's speech in Acts 7 marked a major theological transition in early Christianity by emphasizing that
o: Gentiles must adopt Jewish cultural customs to be saved
God does not dwell exclusively in temples made with hands, transcending physical geography and national boundaries
Moses was a false lawgiver whose writings should be burned
the Jerusalem Temple was the only valid location for divine worship
qs.e: Stephen cited Isaiah 66:1-2 ('Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands...'), preparing the Church to understand Gospel universality beyond Jerusalem.

qs.q: Analyzing Paul's missionary strategy across his three journeys reveals a consistent pattern of first preaching in
o: local Jewish synagogues before turning to Gentiles when official Jewish leadership rejected the message
isolated rural villages before entering major metropolitan cities
pagan marketplace centers before seeking out Jewish communities
royal palaces of Roman governors before speaking to common citizens
qs.e: Acts 13:46, 17:1-2, 18:5-6 illustrate Paul's strategy ('to the Jew first, and also to the Greek'): starting in local synagogues, then expanding to Gentiles when met with synagogue opposition.

qs.q: The core argument of Paul's Epistle to the Romans regarding Abraham's justification (Romans 4) is that Abraham was declared righteous
o: by keeping the written Mosaic Law four hundred years before it was given
only after he was circumcised in Genesis 17
because he offered Isaac on Mount Moriah in Genesis 22
by faith while he was still uncircumcised, proving that justification is by faith apart from legal works for both Jew and Gentile
qs.e: Romans 4:9-11 points out chronologically that Abraham believed God and it was counted as righteousness (Gen 15:6) years before circumcision, establishing justification by faith alone.

qs.q: Harmonizing Paul's doctrine of justification by faith in Romans with James' teaching on faith and works in James 2 shows that
o: Paul and James held contradictory theological views regarding salvation
Paul treats the root of justification before God by faith alone, while James treats the fruit of justification before men through visible works
Paul taught that moral lifestyle choices have no relevance to Christian discipleship
James rejects Christ's substitutionary death in favor of Mosaic legalism
qs.e: Biblical theology reconciles Paul and James: Paul opposes legalistic works as the merit for salvation (Romans 3-4), whereas James opposes dead orthodoxy, showing true faith naturally produces good works (James 2).

qs.q: In James 2:17 & 26, the author emphasizes the practical test of genuine saving faith by declaring that
o: faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone
works alone without faith in Christ yield full justification
faith alone without any behavioral evidence guarantees eternal life
doctrinal knowledge of demonology satisfies divine demands
qs.e: James 2:17 & 26 argues that living, authentic faith inevitably manifests itself in active obedience and good works, just as a body without spirit is dead.

qs.q: In 1 Timothy 6:10, Paul warns Timothy regarding financial temptation by stating that
o: wealth is a mandatory requirement for church eldership
possessing physical money is inherently sinful
the love of money is the root of all evil
qs.e: 1 Timothy 6:10 carefully specifies that 'the love of money' (greed/covetousness), not money itself, is the root of all kinds of evil.

qs.q: A tech startup in Yaba, Lagos, conducts monthly feedback sessions with smartphone users to refine its app features based on customer preferences rather than engineering preference. Which marketing management philosophy is the startup practicing?
qs.e: The marketing concept focuses on determining the needs and wants of target markets and delivering the desired satisfaction more effectively than competitors.

qs.q: An entrepreneur operating a cassava processing plant in Nsukka upgrades waste-water treatment facilities to ensure local streams remain unpolluted, prioritizing community health alongside factory profit. This operational approach represents the
qs.e: The societal marketing concept holds that a company should make marketing decisions considering consumers' wants, company requirements, and long-term societal interests.

qs.q: A boutique hotel in Victoria Island, Lagos, calculates that acquiring a new corporate guest costs N45,000 in digital marketing, whereas retaining an existing corporate client yields N350,000 in net profit over three years. This calculation highlights the strategic value of
qs.e: Customer lifetime value (CLV) quantifies the total net profit a business can expect to earn from a single customer over the entire duration of their relationship.

qs.q: A fitness club owner in Abuja charges a monthly membership fee of N25,000. On average, members stay subscribed for 24 months. If the club's variable cost per member is N7,000 monthly, what is the customer lifetime value (CLV) in profit contribution per member?
qs.e: Monthly profit per member = N25,000 - N7,000 = N18,000. Customer lifetime value = N18,000 x 24 months = N432,000.

qs.q: A commercial bank in Kano trains its branch cashiers and customer care officers on interpersonal courtesy and product knowledge before launching a new high-yield savings product to the public. In holistic marketing, this internal alignment is known as
qs.e: Internal marketing involves hiring, training, and motivating able employees who want to serve customers well, ensuring all staff support marketing goals.

qs.q: When a fast-moving consumer goods firm in Agbara reduces its powdered milk sachet weight from 30g to 26g while keeping the retail price at N100 to offset rising raw material costs, which element of the marketing mix is being adjusted primarily alongside product content?
qs.e: Maintaining the nominal price point while downsizing package content (downsizing) is a strategic price adjustment mechanism to protect profit margins under inflation.

qs.q: In transitioning from the seller-oriented 4 Ps framework to the buyer-oriented 4 Cs model, the 'Place' element corresponds directly to
qs.e: In the 4 Cs framework, Product becomes Customer solution, Price becomes Cost, Place becomes Convenience, and Promotion becomes Communication.

qs.q: A quick-service restaurant chain in Port Harcourt standardizes its kitchen assembly line to reduce customer wait time from 15 minutes to 3 minutes. In the extended marketing mix for services (7 Ps), this improvement represents
qs.e: Process refers to the procedures, mechanisms, and flow of activities by which a service is delivered to the customer efficiently.

qs.q: A logistics and courier company operating in Onitsha equips its delivery drivers with branded uniforms, clean vans, and digital track-and-trace display screens. In service marketing, these tangible touchpoints represent
qs.e: Physical evidence includes the environment in which the service is delivered and any tangible goods that facilitate performance or communication of the service.

qs.q: An edtech firm in Ikeja offers an online video tutoring subscription for N12,000 quarterly. If it spends N3,000 per subscriber on platform server hosting (variable cost) and incurs N1,800,000 in fixed overheads quarterly, how many subscribers are required to achieve break-even in the marketing mix pricing model?
qs.e: Contribution margin per subscriber = N12,000 - N3,000 = N9,000. Break-even subscribers = Fixed Costs / CM = N1,800,000 / N9,000 = 200 subscribers.

qs.q: Sachet drinking water purchased daily by commuters at bus stops in Lagos without prior planning or comparison represents which category of consumer goods?
qs.e: Convenience goods are consumer products that customers purchase frequently, immediately, and with minimal buying effort and store comparison.

qs.q: A hospital in Ibadan purchases an emergency backup 100kVA diesel generator to guarantee uninterrupted power during surgical operations. For the hospital, this generator is classified as
qs.e: Capital items are industrial products that aid in the buyer's production or operations, including installations and major accessory equipment.

qs.q: A conglomerate in Aba manufactures laundry detergents, toilet soaps, dishwashing liquids, and body lotions. The total number of different product lines offered by the company defines its product mix
qs.e: Product mix width (or breadth) refers to the number of different product lines carried by a company.

qs.q: A fruit juice processing firm in Benin City currently sells 1-liter cartons of orange juice and pineapple juice. It introduces a new 250ml sachet variant of orange juice targeted at primary school lunchboxes. This addition is an example of
qs.e: Line extension occurs when a company extends existing brand names to new forms, sizes, or flavors of an existing product category.

qs.q: A solar inverter manufacturer in Asaba offers a basic 3kVA inverter unit for N350,000. For an additional N100,000, it adds a 3-year warranty, free remote mobile monitoring, and annual maintenance visits. These additional features represent which product level?
qs.e: The augmented product includes additional services and benefits built around the core benefit and actual product, such as warranty and after-sales service.

qs.q: A major retail supermarket chain in Abuja sells packaged long-grain rice under its own store name at a price 15% lower than national brands. This packaging strategy is known as a
qs.e: A private label (or store brand) is a brand created and owned by a reseller of a product or service.

qs.q: A conglomerate in Nigeria markets its cement, sugar, salt, and fertilizer under a single corporate name, Dangote. This branding strategy is referred to as
qs.e: Family umbrella branding involves using a single corporate brand name for two or more related or unrelated products in a portfolio.

qs.q: A well-known instant noodle brand in Nigeria leverages its high brand recognition to launch a new line of seasoned potato chips under the exact same brand name. This strategy is an example of
qs.e: Brand extension uses an established brand name to launch a product in a completely new product category.

qs.q: A shopper in Kano enters a provision shop asking specifically for a particular brand of malt drink. When told it is out of stock, the shopper walks past three alternative brands to find another store that stocks their preferred drink. The customer has reached which stage of brand loyalty?
qs.e: Brand insistence is the highest level of brand loyalty where consumers refuse substitutes and will exert substantial effort to buy that specific brand.

qs.q: A premium smartphone manufacturer sells its flagship model for N600,000, while a unbranded generic phone with identical hardware specifications sells for N400,000. The N200,000 price premium consumers are willing to pay solely due to the brand name quantifies the brand's
qs.e: Brand equity is the commercial value derived from consumer perception of the brand name rather than from the product itself, often reflected in premium pricing.

qs.q: The plastic bottle directly holding liquid herbal tea sold in a pharmacy in Jos represents which level of packaging?
qs.e: Primary packaging is the material that directly touches and holds the product, containing it for immediate consumer use.

qs.q: A cardboard box holding 24 individual 1-liter juice cartons for ease of shelf stocking in a supermarket represents
qs.e: Secondary packaging holds multiple primary packages together for protection, display, and handling at the retail store level.

qs.q: Wooden pallets and shrink-wrapped heavy corrugated crates used to transport yam flour across state boundaries from Benue to Lagos are classified as
qs.e: Tertiary (or transit) packaging is designed to protect bulk quantities of goods during bulk shipping, warehousing, and transportation.

qs.q: A seasoning manufacturer in Ogun State package powdered spice into 5g single-use sachets priced at N20 each, enabling low-income rural households to buy exact cooking quantities. This packaging strategy capitalizes primarily on
qs.e: Sachetization breaks bulk into ultra-small affordable units, matching consumer cash flow and expanding market penetration in emerging markets.

qs.q: A cosmetics firm in Lagos redesigns its cream container from a round glass jar to a stackable rectangular plastic tub, reducing master carton shipping volume by 20%. If original freight cost was N500 per unit, what is the new freight cost per unit, assuming freight cost scales linearly with volume?
qs.e: A 20% reduction in volume lowers freight cost by 20%: N500 - (0.20 x N500) = N500 - N100 = N400 per unit.

qs.q: A trader in Ariaria Market, Aba, buys leather shoes for N4,000 per pair and applies a 25% markup on cost. What is the selling price of the shoes?
qs.e: Selling price = Cost + (Cost x Markup %) = N4,000 + (N4,000 x 0.25) = N4,000 + N1,000 = N5,000.

qs.q: If a boutique owner in Ikeja sells a designer dress for N20,000 and earns a profit of N5,000, what is the profit margin percentage on selling price?
qs.e: Profit margin on selling price = (Profit / Selling Price) x 100 = (N5,000 / N20,000) x 100 = 25%.

qs.q: A manufacturer sells goods to a wholesaler with a list price of N50,000, subject to a trade discount of 20% and a cash discount of 5% for payment within 10 days. If the wholesaler pays within 10 days, what is the net amount paid?
qs.e: Price after trade discount = N50,000 x (1 - 0.20) = N40,000. Cash discount = N40,000 x 0.05 = N2,000. Net payment = N40,000 - N2,000 = N38,000.

qs.q: A printing press in Kaduna incurs annual fixed costs of N2,400,000. It prints custom journals sold at N2,000 per unit, with a variable cost of N800 per unit. What is the break-even volume in units?
qs.e: Contribution margin per unit = N2,000 - N800 = N1,200. Break-even quantity = Fixed Costs / CM = N2,400,000 / N1,200 = 2,000 units.

qs.q: A solar home system provider in Enugu faces fixed costs of N3,600,000 annually. Each system sells for N150,000 with variable costs of N90,000 per unit. If the company targets an annual profit of N1,800,000, how many units must be sold?
qs.e: CM per unit = N150,000 - N90,000 = N60,000. Required units = (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) / CM = (N3,600,000 + N1,800,000) / N60,000 = N5,400,000 / N60,000 = 90 units.

qs.q: A poultry farmer in Epe sells fresh eggs directly to consumers at the farm gate without using any middlemen. This distribution network represents a
qs.e: A zero-level channel (direct marketing channel) consists of a manufacturer selling directly to the final consumer without intermediaries.

qs.q: A soft drink manufacturer distributes its products through thousands of roadside kiosks, open market vendors, supermarkets, and street hawkers across Nigeria. This distribution coverage strategy is known as
qs.e: Intensive distribution aims to stock products in as many outlets as possible, essential for convenience items like soft drinks.

qs.q: A luxury Italian suit brand appoints only one authorized retail showroom in Victoria Island, Lagos, to sell its apparel in Nigeria. This distribution coverage is termed
qs.e: Exclusive distribution grants severe limitations on the number of intermediaries, giving one dealer exclusive rights to distribute the brand in a territory.

qs.q: A dispute arising between a soft drink manufacturer and its appointed regional wholesalers over direct factory sales to major retail supermarkets in their territory is an example of
qs.e: Vertical channel conflict occurs between different levels within the same distribution channel (e.g. manufacturer vs wholesaler).

qs.q: A cement factory in Gboko ships cement to Lagos via rail freight at N12,000 per ton (transit time 5 days) or via road haulage at N18,000 per ton (transit time 2 days). If holding cost of inventory in transit is N1,000 per ton per day, which mode yields lower total distribution cost per ton and by how much?
o: Rail freight is cheaper by N3,000
Road haulage is cheaper by N2,000
Rail freight is cheaper by N6,000
Both modes cost exactly the same
qs.e: Rail total cost = Freight N12,000 + Transit inventory (5 days x N1,000 = N5,000) = N17,000. Road total cost = Freight N18,000 + Transit inventory (2 days x N1,000 = N2,000) = N20,000. Rail is cheaper by N20,000 - N17,000 = N3,000.

qs.q: An agricultural chemical firm offers trade allowances and extra free cartons to agro-dealers in Ibadan to persuade them to stock and push its new herbicide to farmers. This promotional strategy is classified as a
qs.e: A push strategy uses the sales force and trade promotion to push the product through marketing channels to final consumers.

qs.q: A soft drink company launches a national radio contest urging consumers to buy bottled drinks, collect caps, and demand prizes from their local provision shops. This strategy is a
qs.e: A pull strategy spends heavily on consumer advertising and promotion to induce final consumers to buy the product, pulling it through channels.

qs.q: A financial services firm in Lagos coordinates its TV commercials, billboard messaging, radio jingles, and social media posts so that all channels communicate a single unified brand message. This strategic approach is called
qs.e: Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) carefully integrates and coordinates company communication channels to deliver a clear, consistent message.

qs.q: In the AIDA model of promotional communication, what does the second letter 'I' represent?
qs.e: The AIDA model stands for Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action.

qs.q: A consumer goods company sets its annual promotional budget at exactly 5% of its projected annual gross sales revenue of N800,000,000. What is the allocated promotional budget?
An advertising campaign launched by a solar inverter firm in Enugu aims primarily to educate rural off-grid shopkeepers on how solar power operates. This campaign is categorized as
qs.e: Informative advertising is heavily used when introducing a new product category to build primary demand and educate consumers.

qs.q: A radio station in Ibadan charges N150,000 for a 30-second advert spot during peak morning commute hours, reaching an estimated audience of 500,000 listeners. What is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) for this radio advert?
qs.e: CPM = (Cost of Advert / Total Audience) x 1,000 = (N150,000 / 500,000) x 1,000 = N0.30 x 1,000 = N300.

qs.q: An established malt drink brand runs commercials during festive seasons simply displaying cold bottles with cheerful holiday music without mentioning product features. This form of advertising is
qs.e: Reminder advertising is important for mature products to keep consumers thinking about the product.

qs.q: A media buyer evaluates two radio stations in Lagos: Station A charges N400,000 per advert spot with 1,600,000 listeners; Station B charges N250,000 per spot with 800,000 listeners. Which station offers the lower CPM and by how much?
o: Station A is cheaper by N62.50
Station B is cheaper by N50.00
Station A is cheaper by N125.00
Both stations have the same CPM

qs.q: The statutory body in Nigeria responsible for regulating advertising practice, controlling advert contents, and conducting pre-exposure vetting of advertisements is the
qs.e: ARCON (Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria, formerly APCON) regulates advertising practice and advertisement vetting in Nigeria.

qs.q: In the personal selling process, a sales representative who researches a prospective corporate client's financial background and executive structure before making initial contact is engaged in
qs.e: Pre-approach is the step in which the salesperson learns as much as possible about a prospective customer before making a sales call.

qs.q: When a prospective buyer in Kano says 'Your solar inverter is too expensive,' and the salesperson replies 'While the initial cost is higher, it eliminates generator fuel costs and pays for itself within 12 months,' the salesperson is executing which selling step?
qs.e: Handling objections is the step in which the salesperson seeks out, clarifies, and overcomes customer objections to buying.

qs.q: A commercial sales representative in Lagos receives a monthly base salary of N100,000 plus a 5% commission on total sales exceeding N2,000,000. If the representative generates N4,500,000 in sales in a month, what is their total monthly earnings?
qs.e: Eligible sales for commission = N4,500,000 - N2,000,000 = N2,500,000. Commission = 5% of N2,500,000 = N125,000. Total earnings = N100,000 base + N125,000 commission = N200,000.

qs.q: A firm assigns its sales representatives exclusive geographical territories across Southwestern Nigeria, expecting each representative to sell the firm's entire product line to all customers in that territory. This organizational design is a
qs.e: A territorial sales force structure assigns each salesperson an exclusive geographic territory in which that salesperson sells the company's full line.

qs.q: An industrial machinery supplier in Port Harcourt estimates that it has 400 key accounts requiring 15 sales visits per year each. If a full-time sales representative can complete 300 client visits per year, how many sales representatives are needed under the workload method?
qs.e: Total annual calls required = 400 accounts x 15 visits = 6,000 calls. Sales force size = Total calls / Calls per rep = 6,000 / 300 = 20 representatives.

qs.q: A supermarket in Lekki, Lagos, attaches a free plastic mixing bowl to every 2kg bag of cake flour purchased. This sales promotion technique is classified as a
qs.e: A premium is a good offered either free or at low cost as an incentive to buy a product.

qs.q: An instant noodle company prints unique scratch codes inside promo wrappers, allowing buyers to text codes and win instant cash prizes or cars. This promotional scheme is a
qs.e: Contests and sweepstakes offer consumers the chance to win something such as cash, trips, or goods by luck or extra effort.

qs.q: A soft drink manufacturer offers retail shop owners in Onitsha 1 extra free carton for every 10 cartons purchased in cash during a holiday promotion. This trade incentive is known as
qs.e: Free goods are offers of extra cases of merchandise to intermediaries who buy certain quantities or who feature a certain flavor or size.

qs.q: An electronics brand pays retail sales assistants in computer stores N1,000 cash for every unit of its premium laptop sold during a quarter. In trade promotion, this cash incentive is called
qs.e: Push money (or a spiff) is cash or gifts given to dealers or their sales force to push the manufacturer's goods.

qs.q: A retail store sells 500 units of a beverage per month at N1,000 each (gross margin 30%). During a 1-month promotion, it slashes the price by 10% to N900, causing volume to increase to 800 units. If unit cost remains N700, did total gross profit increase or decrease and by how much?
qs.e: Pre-promo gross profit = 500 units x (N1,000 - N700) = 500 x N300 = N150,000. Promo gross profit = 800 units x (N900 - N700) = 800 x N200 = N160,000. Profit increased by N160,000 - N150,000 = N10,000.

qs.q: An oil processing company in Port Harcourt builds modern community health centers and sinks borehole wells in host villages to foster goodwill and peaceful operating relations. This activity represents
qs.e: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) and community relations build positive goodwill with external stakeholders and local communities.

qs.q: Following a rumor on social media regarding product contamination, a beverage firm holds an immediate press conference with regulatory officials and releases laboratory certificates proving safety. This action exemplifies
qs.e: Crisis management involves swift, transparent public relations handling to mitigate damage to brand reputation during negative events.

qs.q: A commercial bank sponsors the annual Lagos City Marathon, placing its logo on runner bibs, banners, and national TV broadcasts. This promotional investment is an example of
qs.e: Event sponsorship builds brand exposure and positive public relations by linking the company to popular sporting or cultural events.

qs.q: The primary strategic advantage of public relations and publicity over paid television advertising is its
qs.e: Publicity carries higher message credibility because news stories and features seem more authentic and believable to readers than paid ads.

qs.q: A bottled water company pledges to donate N5 from every 75cl bottle sold during the dry season to fund rural borehole drilling in arid northern communities. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Cause-related marketing directly links product sales to raising funds for a specific charitable or social cause.

qs.q: A cosmetic brand in Lagos formulates distinct product lines specifically for teenagers, working professional women, and elderly consumers based on age brackets. This market segmentation basis is
qs.e: Demographic segmentation divides the market into groups based on variables such as age, gender, family size, income, occupation, and education.

qs.q: An energy drink manufacturer targets long-distance commercial drivers, night-shift factory workers, and university students studying for exams based on product usage occasions and lifestyle. This segmentation is
qs.e: Psychographic segmentation divides buyers based on social class, lifestyle, or personality; behavioral segmentation divides based on occasions or usage.

qs.q: A boutique footwear producer in Aba focuses exclusively on custom hand-crafted leather boots for men with shoe sizes 46 and above. This target marketing strategy represents
qs.e: Concentrated (or niche) marketing targets a large share of one or a few smaller segments or niches.

qs.q: A salt refining company packages a single standard grade of iodized salt in identical 500g plastic bags sold nationwide without variation in price or marketing message. This approach is
qs.e: Undifferentiated (mass) marketing targets the whole market with one offer, ignoring segment differences.

qs.q: To be effective and actionable for a business, a market segment must fulfill five key criteria. When a segment is rejected because it contains too few consumers to generate sufficient profit, it fails which criterion?
qs.e: Substantiality requires that market segments are large or profitable enough to serve.

qs.q: What is the first step in the consumer buying decision process when a householder notices that their cooking gas cylinder is completely empty?
qs.e: The buying process starts with problem or need recognition, where the buyer senses a difference between their actual state and desired state.

qs.q: A consumer experiences psychological discomfort, anxiety, and second-guessing shortly after making an expensive purchase of a N450,000 solar generator. In consumer behavior, this state is called
qs.e: Cognitive dissonance is buyer discomfort caused by post-purchase conflict, where the buyer doubts whether they made the correct choice.

qs.q: When buying household table salt at a local neighborhood store, a shopper picks whichever brand is on the counter without comparing ingredients or price. This buying behavior is classified as
qs.e: Habitual buying behavior occurs under conditions of low consumer involvement and little significant brand difference.

qs.q: A teenager in Ibadan insists on purchasing a specific brand of basketball sneakers primarily because their favorite musical artist and school friends wear them. In consumer behavior, the musician and peer group act as a
qs.e: A reference group serves as a direct or indirect point of comparison or reference in forming a person's attitudes or behavior.

qs.q: According to Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, purchasing a home security alarm system and emergency backup battery in a residential estate fulfills primarily which level of human needs?
qs.e: Safety needs encompass security, protection, stability, and freedom from fear or threat.

qs.q: Before embarking on expensive field surveys, a marketing research officer in Lagos collects population census figures, CBN economic bulletins, and published trade reports. These data sources are classified as
qs.e: Secondary data consists of information that already exists somewhere, having been collected for another purpose.

qs.q: A research team invites 8 mothers in Kano to a conference room to discuss their perceptions, preferences, and feeding habits regarding infant cereals under the guidance of a trained moderator. This research method is a
qs.e: A focus group interview involves personal interviewing of 6 to 10 people for a few hours with a trained moderator to talk about a product or service.

qs.q: A supermarket researcher in Ibadan counts the exact number of shoppers who stop by the dairy display case and records how many pick up a specific brand without speaking to the shoppers. This data collection technique is
qs.e: Observational research gathers primary data by observing relevant people, actions, and situations.

qs.q: A field researcher selects every 10th shopper entering a shopping mall in Enugu from a starting random point until 100 interviews are completed. This sampling method is known as
qs.e: Systematic sampling selects sample members from a target population according to a random starting point and a fixed, periodic interval.

qs.q: An e-commerce firm in Yaba tests two different landing page layouts (Version A with a red buy button, Version B with a green buy button) by randomly directing 5,000 visitors to each version and comparing purchase rates. This research methodology is an
qs.e: Experimental research gathers primary data by selecting matched groups of subjects, giving them different treatments, controlling factors, and checking differences in group responses.

qs.q: An empty seat on an early morning flight from Abuja to Lagos cannot be stored in inventory for resale on the evening flight if it goes unsold. This service characteristic is known as
qs.e: Perishability means that services cannot be stored for later sale or use.

qs.q: A patient cannot inspect, touch, or test a physician's medical consultation before paying for and receiving the clinical checkup. This service characteristic represents
qs.e: Intangibility means services cannot be seen, tasted, felt, heard, or smelled before they are bought.

qs.q: A barber cutting a client's hair in a salon in Kaduna performs the service while the client simultaneously consumes it. This characteristic is termed
qs.e: Inseparability means services are produced and consumed at the same time and cannot be separated from their providers.

qs.q: The quality of service delivered at a hotel front desk in Calabar varies depending on which receptionist is on duty and their energy level during the shift. This service characteristic is
qs.e: Variability (heterogeneity) means that the quality of services depends on who provides them, as well as when, where, and how they are provided.

qs.q: In the SERVQUAL framework for assessing service quality, when a customer rates a logistics firm highly because it delivers shipments accurately on the promised date without errors, which dimension is being demonstrated?
qs.e: Reliability refers to the ability to perform the promised service dependably and accurately.

qs.q: An online shoe store in Lagos spends N200,000 on social media ads, generating 10,000 ad clicks that result in 250 completed shoe purchases. What is the e-commerce conversion rate?
qs.e: Conversion rate = (Number of conversions / Total clicks) x 100 = (250 / 10,000) x 100 = 2.5%.

qs.q: A digital agency runs a search engine campaign for a real estate firm in Abuja, spending N600,000 in total. The campaign yields 30 qualified property buyer leads. What is the Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) per lead?
qs.e: Cost Per Acquisition = Total Ad Spend / Total Conversions = N600,000 / 30 = N20,000.

qs.q: Optimizing website text, mobile responsiveness, and page loading speed so a company ranks at the top of unpaid organic search engine results is called
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) improves website traffic quality and volume from organic (unpaid) search results.

qs.q: An online clothing retailer pays a fashion influencer a 10% commission on every sale tracked through a unique promotional link shared on the influencer's social media profile. This digital marketing strategy is
qs.e: Affiliate marketing pays third-party publishers (affiliates) a commission to generate traffic or leads to the company's products.

qs.q: An online marketplace where individual consumers list and sell used personal items directly to other consumers, such as Jiji or eBay, operates under which e-commerce business model?
qs.e: Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) e-commerce involves commercial transactions between private individuals.

qs.q: A newly introduced electric vehicle brand in Nigeria experiences high promotional expenses, negative net profits, and slow sales growth while educating early adopters. The brand is in which stage of the product lifecycle?
qs.e: The introduction stage is characterized by slow sales growth, high launch costs, and non-existent or negative profits.

qs.q: A fintech mobile payment solution experiences rapid market acceptance, surging sales revenues, rising profits, and the emergence of several new competitive copycat apps. This product is in the
qs.e: The growth stage features rapid market acceptance, escalating sales volume, increasing profits, and new competitors entering the market.

qs.q: The sachet water industry in Nigeria exhibits saturated consumer demand, intense price competition among hundreds of local producers, stable sales volume, and squeezed profit margins. This product category is in the
qs.e: The maturity stage is marked by slowdown in sales growth, saturation of market demand, fierce price competition, and industry consolidation.

qs.q: Demand for standalone DVD players in Nigeria drops drastically as consumers switch to internet streaming and flash drives. Manufacturers scale back ad budgets and harvest remaining sales. DVD players are in the
qs.e: The decline stage occurs when sales drop significantly due to technological shifts, consumer taste changes, or increased competition.

qs.q: To extend the lifecycle of a mature malt drink brand experiencing flat sales, the manufacturer formulates a low-sugar variant and launches an export campaign to neighboring ECOWAS countries. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Modifying the product (new features/variants) and modifying the market (new geographic segments) are classic techniques to extend the PLC during maturity.

qs.q: Demand for industrial corrugated packaging boxes in Aba surges sharply because consumer market demand for packaged biscuits and soaps increases. In industrial marketing, this phenomenon is called
qs.e: Derived demand is business demand that ultimately comes from (derives from) the demand for consumer goods.

qs.q: An administrative receptionist at a corporate head office in Lagos routinely screens phone calls and blocks sales representatives from scheduling meetings with the Chief Procurement Officer. In the organizational buying center, the receptionist acts as a
qs.e: Gatekeepers control the flow of information to others in the organizational buying center.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant manager in Ibadan reorders 100 reams of A4 printing paper from an existing supplier under pre-negotiated price and delivery terms without modifications. This organizational buying situation is a
qs.e: A straight rebuy is a business buying situation in which the buyer routinely reorders something without any modifications.

qs.q: A private university in Abuja decides to replace its desktop computer labs with laptops, inviting quotes from 4 vendors to revise specifications, pricing, and warranty terms. This purchase is a
qs.e: A modified rebuy occurs when a business buyer wants to modify product specifications, prices, terms, or suppliers.

qs.q: A commercial flour mill in Kano agrees to purchase all its grain transport trucks from an auto assembly plant in Kaduna, provided the assembly plant purchases all its staff canteen baked bread flour from the Kano mill. This B2B purchasing arrangement is
qs.e: Reciprocal buying involves two organizations agreeing to buy each other's products and services.

qs.q: A Nigerian fast-food company expands into Ghana by granting a local Accra entrepreneur the legal right to use its brand name, recipes, and operating systems in exchange for an upfront fee and ongoing royalties. This market entry mode is
qs.e: Franchising is a contractual association between a franchisor and an independent franchisee who buys the right to own and operate units in the franchise system.

qs.q: A footwear manufacturer in Aba partners with a distribution firm in Togo to build a shared warehouse and retail chain in Lome, sharing equity capital, operational control, and financial risks equally. This market entry mode is a
qs.e: A joint venture is a commercial enterprise undertaken jointly by two or more businesses which otherwise retain their distinct identities, sharing capital and risks.

qs.q: A global fast-food brand entering Nigeria adjusts its menu by replacing pork items with halal beef and introducing spicy jollof rice options to match local cultural preferences. This strategy is known as
qs.e: Product adaptation involves altering a product to meet local conditions, cultural preferences, or legal requirements in international markets.

qs.q: The regional trade agreement that enables goods originating within ECOWAS member states to move duty-free across West African borders without import tariffs is the
qs.e: The ECOWAS Trade Liberalization Scheme (ETLS) is the main regional trade instrument aimed at encouraging free movement of goods originating in West Africa.

qs.q: A Nigerian importer orders N40,000,000 worth of electrical appliances from a supplier in Europe invoiced in Euros. If the Naira depreciates by 15% against the Euro before payment is settled, how much additional Naira must the importer pay to clear the invoice?
qs.e: Additional Naira cost due to 15% currency depreciation = 15% of N40,000,000 = 0.15 x N40,000,000 = N6,000,000.

qs.q: A motor spare parts manufacturer in Nnewi invests heavily in expanding foundry production capacity to 50,000 units per month, assuming that producing at maximum volume and lowest cost will automatically guarantee sales. The manufacturer is demonstrating the
qs.e: The production concept holds that consumers favor products that are available and highly affordable, leading management to focus on production efficiency.

qs.q: A cosmetics company in Ikeja sells a luxury skin cream for N15,000 per jar. The total manufacturing and packaging cost is N6,000. If the customer perceives total tangible and intangible benefits worth N20,000, what is the customer perceived value (net value benefit)?
qs.e: Customer perceived value = Total perceived benefit - Total customer cost (price paid) = N20,000 - N15,000 = N5,000.

qs.q: A railway corporation in Enugu defines its business strictly as 'running train tracks and engines' rather than 'providing passenger and freight transportation solutions'. When bus fleets and airline shuttles capture its market share, the railway suffers from
qs.e: Marketing myopia is short-sighted inward management focus on products rather than on broader customer needs and solutions.

qs.q: An electricity distribution company (DisCo) in Abuja launches a public campaign urging consumers to turn off air conditioners and water heaters during peak evening hours to prevent power grid overload. This strategic effort to reduce demand temporarily is known as
qs.e: Demarketing aims to reduce demand temporarily or permanently, not to destroy demand but only to reduce or shift it.

qs.q: A state ministry of health in Kano runs aggressive radio adverts and billboard campaigns highlighting the organ damage caused by unprescribed cough syrup abuse to eradicate its consumption completely. This approach represents
qs.e: Counter-marketing seeks to destroy unwholesome or harmful demand completely (such as for dangerous drugs, tobacco, or alcohol).

qs.q: A soft drink bottling plant in Ibadan increases its 35cl bottle retail price from N150 to N200. As a result, weekly sales drop from 10,000 cases to 8,000 cases. What is the price elasticity of demand coefficient for the soft drink?
qs.e: Percentage change in price = (200 - 150) / 150 = +33.33%. Percentage change in quantity = (8,000 - 10,000) / 10,000 = -20.0%. Elasticity = -20% / 33.33% = -0.60.

qs.q: An e-commerce mobile application platform operating in Yaba redesigned its user checkout workflow, reducing payment button taps from 6 clicks to 2 clicks. In the customer-centric 4 Cs framework, this improvement enhances customer
qs.e: Convenience in the 4 Cs framework corresponds to Place in the 4 Ps, focusing on ease of acquiring and transacting.

qs.q: A high-end private medical clinic in Abuja installs marble flooring, soft acoustic lighting, plush leather recliners, and complimentary refreshments in its waiting lounge. In the 7 Ps services mix, these physical elements constitute
qs.e: Physical evidence includes the physical environment where the service is provided and tangible touchpoints that reinforce service quality perceptions.

qs.q: A commercial air conditioning installer in Port Harcourt bundles a 2-year free servicing contract and free electrical cabling with every unit purchased for N400,000. How does this service addition modify the product offering in the marketing mix?
qs.e: Free servicing and installation accessories build around the basic product to create an augmented product offering superior value.

qs.q: A manufacturer of fruit juices sells 50,000 cartons monthly at N4,000 per carton. If variable production cost is N2,500 per carton and monthly fixed marketing expenses are N45,000,000, what is the net monthly operating profit?
qs.e: Total contribution margin = 50,000 cartons x (N4,000 - N2,500) = 50,000 x N1,500 = N75,000,000. Net profit = Total CM - Fixed Expenses = N75,000,000 - N45,000,000 = N30,000,000.

qs.q: A civil engineering contractor in Abuja purchases bulk cement bags, steel rebar rods, and gravel for bridge construction. In industrial product classification, these materials are
qs.e: Materials and parts are industrial goods that enter the manufacturer's product completely, including raw materials and fabricated parts.

qs.q: A furniture manufacturer in Benin City introduces a new modular office desk series with 6 color options and 4 drawer configurations under its existing executive desk line. This expansion increases the product line's
qs.e: Product line depth refers to the number of versions or variants offered of each product in the line.

qs.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer in Onitsha reformulates its pediatric syrup by removing artificial colorings and adding a child-resistant safety cap. This action represents
qs.e: Product modification involves changing one or more characteristics of a product (quality, functional, or aesthetic features).

qs.q: An FMCG firm in Ogun State launches a low-priced sachet variant of its popular tin milk. Within six months, 40% of sachet milk buyers are existing buyers who stopped purchasing the higher-margin tin milk. This phenomenon is known as
qs.e: Product cannibalization occurs when a new product eats into the sales volume and market share of an existing product from the same company.

qs.q: A consumer buys a 55-inch smart television in Jos primarily to watch football matches in high definition. The basic core need fulfilled by this purchase is classified as the
qs.e: The core benefit is the fundamental service or need that the consumer is truly buying (e.g. entertainment/viewing experience).

qs.q: A multinational company markets Ariel detergent, Pampers diapers, and Always sanitary pads in Nigeria without prominently displaying its corporate parent name on the front packages. This branding strategy is
qs.e: Individual branding uses distinct brand names for each product in a company's portfolio, protecting the corporate reputation if one product fails.

qs.q: A commercial bank and an international airline collaborate to issue a joint credit card that earns frequent flyer miles whenever spent. This partnership is an example of
qs.e: Co-branding occurs when two established brand names of different companies are used on the same product.

qs.q: A major commercial bank in Nigeria changes its corporate logo, changes its branch interior colors, and adopts the tagline 'Empowering Your Future' to refresh its market image among young tech workers. This strategic action is
qs.e: Rebranding is the creation of a new name, term, symbol, design, or combination for an established brand to develop a new identity.

qs.q: A luxury leather shoe maker in Aba decides to put its brand name on low-cost plastic flip-flops sold for N500 at roadside stalls. Existing customers perceive the brand as less exclusive, resulting in
qs.e: Brand dilution occurs when a brand extension adversely affects consumer perceptions about the attributes or quality of the core brand.

qs.q: In a market survey conducted in Computer Village, Ikeja, 85 out of 100 shoppers correctly identify a mobile phone brand's logo without seeing the brand name. This percentage measures
qs.e: Brand recognition is the ability of consumers to confirm prior exposure to the brand when given the brand as a cue.

qs.q: A tamper-evident metallic foil seal placed across the mouth of a plastic medicine bottle in a pharmacy serves primarily which packaging function?
qs.e: Tamper-evident seals provide protection, preventing contamination and assuring consumers of safety and product integrity.

qs.q: A food processing firm prints nutritional facts, NAFDAC registration numbers, batch codes, and expiry dates on the back of its packaged oats. This fulfills which function of packaging?
qs.e: Labeling provides crucial consumer information regarding ingredients, usage, and legal compliance required by regulatory agencies like NAFDAC.

qs.q: A biscuit manufacturer designs an ornate metal tin container for its holiday cookies so that consumers will reuse the tin as a household storage box after eating the cookies. This packaging design is known as
qs.e: Dual-use (or reusable) packaging is designed to be repurposed by consumers for other household uses after the original contents are consumed.

qs.q: In a self-service supermarket in Port Harcourt, a brightly colored product package with bold typography acts as a 'silent salesman'. Which primary function of packaging does this illustrate?
qs.e: Packaging acts as a silent salesman on self-service supermarket shelves by attracting attention, describing the product, and making the sale.

qs.q: A cooking oil refiner in Kano replaces heavy glass bottles with lightweight PET plastic bottles, reducing package tare weight per case from 2.5kg to 0.5kg. If a delivery truck transports 1,000 cases, how many total kilograms of dead weight are saved during transport?
qs.e: Tare weight saved per case = 2.5kg - 0.5kg = 2.0kg. Total dead weight saved = 1,000 cases x 2.0kg = 2,000 kg.

qs.q: A boutique owner buys a handbag for N12,000 and wants to achieve a 20% profit margin on the selling price. What must be the selling price of the handbag?
qs.e: Selling price S = Cost / (1 - Margin %) = N12,000 / (1 - 0.20) = N12,000 / 0.80 = N15,000. Profit = N3,000 (which is 20% of N15,000).

qs.q: A tech firm introducing a revolutionary foldable smartphone sets an initial price of N1,200,000 to maximize short-term revenue from tech enthusiasts before lowering price over time. This pricing strategy is
qs.e: Market-skimming pricing sets a high initial price for a new product to skim maximum revenues layer by layer from segments willing to pay.

qs.q: A supermarket in Ibadan prices boxed chocolates at N4,999 instead of N5,000. This pricing tactic relies on which psychological principle?
qs.e: Odd pricing uses prices ending in odd numbers (like .99 or 9) to make the price seem significantly lower than it is.

qs.q: A printer manufacturer sells desktop laser printers at a break-even price of N35,000 but sets a high profit margin on replacement toner cartridges. This strategy is
qs.e: Captive product pricing sets a low price for the main product and a high markup on goods that must be used with the main product.

qs.q: A cinema in Ikeja charges N2,500 for adult evening tickets and N1,500 for student afternoon tickets for the exact same movie screening. This pricing practice is known as
qs.e: Segmented pricing (price discrimination) sells a product or service at two or more prices, where the difference in prices is not based on differences in costs.

qs.q: A fashion designer in Lagos sells bespoke dresses exclusively through an e-commerce website and social media messaging directly to individual buyers. This distribution network is a
qs.e: Direct distribution channels sell products directly from the producer to final consumers without independent intermediaries.

qs.q: A major wholesaler in Bodija Market, Ibadan, purchases 5,000 bags of rice from processing mills, stores them in central warehouses, and sells 10-bag bundles to small neighbourhood retailers. Which key channel function is the wholesaler performing?
qs.e: Wholesalers perform bulk breaking by purchasing large quantities and breaking them down into smaller lots for retailers.

qs.q: A corporate food company in Lagos bypasses independent regional wholesalers and begins selling directly to major supermarket chains. The elimination of wholesalers from the distribution chain is called
qs.e: Disintermediation is the cutting out of marketing channel intermediaries by product or service producers or the displacement of traditional resellers.

qs.q: A petroleum refining company transports refined PMS fuel from Port Harcourt to Kaduna via an underground pipeline rather than road tankers. The primary operational advantage of pipeline transport is
o: Fastest delivery speed for small lots
qs.e: Pipelines provide continuous, automated, high-volume physical transport for liquid petroleum products at very low variable costs per unit.

qs.q: A distributor in Onitsha holds N50,000,000 in average inventory. Annual inventory holding cost rate is 18%. By implementing a just-in-time (JIT) replenishment system, average inventory is reduced to N30,000,000. How much annual inventory holding cost is saved?
qs.e: Inventory reduction = N50,000,000 - N30,000,000 = N20,000,000. Annual holding cost savings = 18% of N20,000,000 = 0.18 x N20,000,000 = N3,600,000.

qs.q: A new solar home kit company runs heavy television ads and sponsors radio talk shows to build brand awareness among suburban homeowners in Ogun State. Which element of the promotional mix is primarily utilized?
qs.e: Advertising is any paid form of non-personal presentation and promotion of ideas, goods, or services by an identified sponsor.

qs.q: A telecommunications company sends targeted SMS text messages with personalized recharge discount offers directly to registered subscribers. This strategy is an example of
qs.e: Direct marketing involves engaging directly with carefully targeted individual consumers to obtain an immediate response and cultivate lasting relationships.

qs.q: When setting promotional budgets, a company that allocates marketing funds to match the estimated promotional expenditures of its main industry competitors is using the
qs.e: The competitive-parity method sets promotion budgets to match competitors' outlays.

qs.q: The most thorough and logically defensive method for establishing a marketing promotion budget, which defines specific campaign objectives, identifies required tasks, and estimates associated costs, is the
qs.e: The objective-and-task method develops promotion budgets by defining specific objectives, determining tasks required, and estimating costs.

qs.q: In communication theory applied to advertising, when a radio listener in Enugu misinterprets a promotional tagline due to localized language dialect differences, which element of the communication process has failed?
qs.e: Decoding is the process by which the receiver assigns meaning to the symbols encoded by the sender; misinterpretation represents a decoding error.

qs.q: An oil marketing company sponsors an educational television documentary on environmental conservation without promoting any specific fuel brand. This advert is categorized as
qs.e: Institutional (corporate) advertising promotes the corporate image, reputation, or social contributions rather than a specific product.

qs.q: A billboard advert for an insect repellent shows a mother smiling peacefully while her sleeping baby is protected under a net, appealing to maternal protective instincts. This advertisement uses an
qs.e: Emotional appeals attempt to stir up negative or positive emotions (such as love, safety, fear, or pride) to motivate purchase.

qs.q: A media planner schedules television commercials to run at steady, continuous levels every week throughout the year. This media scheduling pattern is known as
qs.e: Continuous scheduling runs advertising at an even, continuous schedule over a given period.

qs.q: An ad agency charges N1,200,000 to produce a 30-second video ad and N800,000 to air it on regional TV reaching 2,500,000 viewers. What is the total CPM including production and media costs?
In an advertising agency, the professional responsible for negotiating and purchasing billboard slots, television airtime, and radio ad schedules is the
qs.e: The media buyer negotiates and purchases advertising time and space across various media channels.

qs.q: A sales representative calling on a commercial bakery in Ibadan presents cost comparison charts showing how switching to their commercial baking oven saves N80,000 monthly in gas. This step in personal selling is the
qs.e: Presentation and demonstration is the personal selling step where the salesperson tells the 'value story' to the buyer, showing how the offer solves problems.

qs.q: After delivering a comprehensive presentation on industrial solar panels, a salesperson asks: 'Would you prefer installation to begin this Monday or next Thursday?' This sales technique is an example of an
qs.e: An assumptive close assumes the customer has already decided to buy and asks for secondary choices like delivery dates.

qs.q: Two weeks after installing a commercial generator at a hotel in Enugu, the sales representative visits the hotel engineer to verify performance and answer questions. This personal selling step is
qs.e: Follow-up is the last step in the selling process in which the salesperson follows up after the sale to ensure customer satisfaction and repeat business.

qs.q: A B2B sales team is organized such that dedicated sales representatives sell exclusively to agricultural clients, while another set sells exclusively to educational institutions. This structure is a
qs.e: A customer (or market) sales force structure organizes salespeople along customer or industry lines.

qs.q: A field salesperson receives a fixed salary of N150,000 plus a commission of 4% on all sales generated. If the salesperson achieves N6,000,000 in monthly sales, what percentage of their total earnings comes from commissions?
qs.e: Commission = 4% of N6,000,000 = N240,000. Total earnings = N150,000 + N240,000 = N390,000. Percentage from commission = (N240,000 / N390,000) x 100 = 61.54% ~ 61.5%.

qs.q: A manufacturer of dishwashing liquid places a N100 instant discount sticker on the front of its 1-liter bottle in supermarkets across Abuja. This promotional tactic is a
qs.e: Price-off deals (cents-off/naira-off) offer consumers savings off the regular price directly marked on the label or package.

qs.q: A coffee shop chain in Victoria Island issues loyalty stamp cards where customers receive a free coffee after buying 9 cups. This promotional mechanism is designed primarily to promote
qs.e: Frequency / loyalty programs reward customers who buy frequently or in large amounts to encourage repeat purchase behavior.

qs.q: A trade exhibition held annually at the Lagos International Trade Fair Complex allows B2B heavy machinery suppliers to demonstrate tractors to agricultural cooperative representatives. This event functions as a
qs.e: Trade shows and conventions are business promotional events where firms exhibit products to industry buyers and build B2B relationships.

qs.q: A beverage firm agrees to reimburse 50% of the cost of local newspaper advertisements placed by independent retail distributors featuring its fruit juice brand. This financial support is called
qs.e: Cooperative advertising allowances are trade incentives where a manufacturer pays a percentage of the retailer's local advertising costs.

qs.q: A consumer products firm spending N20,000,000 on a sales promotion generates N50,000,000 in incremental sales volume. If unit gross profit margin is 35%, what is the net return on investment (ROI) percentage of the sales promotion campaign?
A major corporate bank publishes a quarterly employee magazine and hosts monthly town hall meetings with staff to build internal culture and alignment. These activities fall under
qs.e: Internal PR focuses on building positive relationships, communication channels, and shared values among company employees.

qs.q: An association of local poultry farmers in Nigeria engages policy consultants to meet with federal legislators to advocate against reducing tariffs on imported frozen chicken. This activity is
qs.e: Lobbying involves dealing with legislators and government officials to promote or defeat regulation and legislation.

qs.q: A public relations officer prepares a written news announcement regarding the commissioning of a new factory line in Sagamu and emails it to national newspaper editors. This document is a
qs.e: A press (or news) release is a brief, written summary sent to media outlets to announce news events or developments.

qs.q: A tech corporation donates 500 refurbished laptops to public secondary schools in Kano State. Journalists cover the handover ceremony on national news. The resulting media coverage is classified as
qs.e: Earned media (publicity) is news coverage or editorial mention gained through promotional efforts rather than paid advertising.

qs.q: When evaluating the financial equivalent value of public relations coverage, PR managers calculate the cost of purchasing equivalent advertising space for news articles. This metric is known as
qs.e: Advertising Value Equivalency (AVE) measures the benefit to a client from media coverage by calculating what that coverage would cost as paid advertising.

qs.q: A clothing manufacturer produces heavy wool coats for customers in cold mountain regions like Jos and light cotton shirts for humid coastal cities like Lagos. This segmentation approach is
qs.e: Geographic segmentation divides the market into different geographical units such as nations, regions, states, cities, or climate zones.

qs.q: A toothpaste brand offers four versions: one for tooth whitening, one for sensitive gums, one for fresh breath, and one for decay protection. This market segmentation is based on
qs.e: Benefit segmentation divides buyers according to the different benefits that they seek from the product.

qs.q: An airline categorizes its passenger database into 'Frequent Flyers' (heavy users who generate 70% of revenue) and 'Occasional Holiday Travelers' (light users). This breakdown is an example of
qs.e: Usage rate segmentation classifies buyers into light, medium, and heavy product users.

qs.q: A commercial bank designs distinct financial packages: 'SME Commercial Current Account' for business owners, 'Campus Student Account' for undergraduates, and 'Private Wealth Account' for high-net-worth individuals. This target marketing strategy is
qs.e: Differentiated (segmented) marketing targets several market segments and designs separate offers for each.

qs.q: Plotting consumer perceptions of rival mobile phone brands on a two-dimensional grid representing 'Price' on one axis and 'Battery Performance' on the other axis creates a
qs.e: A perceptual (or positioning) map visually displays consumer perceptions of competing brands along key purchasing dimensions.

qs.q: A buyer evaluating three competing refrigerator brands in an appliance store in Aba weighs cooling speed, power consumption, and warranty duration before making a final choice. The buyer is in which decision stage?
qs.e: In the evaluation of alternatives stage, consumers evaluate different brand choices based on specific product criteria and attributes.

qs.q: A shopper in a supermarket notices that a candy bar's net weight was reduced from 50g to 48g without altering the package size, but fails to notice the change. In sensory psychology applied to marketing, the 2g difference was below the consumer's
qs.e: The Just Noticeable Difference (JND) or differential threshold is the minimal difference that can be detected between two similar stimuli.

qs.q: When a consumer hears a television advert for a product they dislike, they unconsciously re-interpret the spokesperson's words to fit their pre-existing negative bias. This perceptual process is called
qs.e: Selective distortion describes the tendency of people to interpret information in a way that supports what they already believe.

qs.q: A household buying decision for a new family car involves the teenage daughter suggesting an SUV model, the father reviewing financing options, and the mother making the final brand decision. In buying roles, the mother is the
qs.e: The decider is the person who ultimately makes the buying decision or any part of it (whether to buy, what to buy, how to buy, or where to buy).

qs.q: A consumer switches from buying Brand A biscuits to Brand B biscuits not because Brand A was bad, but simply out of curiosity to try a new taste. This purchase behavior is
qs.e: Variety-seeking buying behavior occurs in situations characterized by low consumer involvement but significant perceived brand differences, leading to frequent brand switching for novelty.

qs.q: A market research agency in Lagos collects field survey data specifically to answer a client's question regarding customer satisfaction with a new telco data plan. This freshly gathered data is classified as
qs.e: Primary data consists of information collected for the specific purpose at hand.

qs.q: Dividing a city's population into distinct income subgroups (Low, Middle, High income) and randomly selecting 50 households from each subgroup ensures balanced representation. This sampling technique is
qs.e: Stratified random sampling divides the population into mutually exclusive groups (strata) and draws random samples from each stratum.

qs.q: A questionnaire item that asks: 'Do you agree that our product is cheap and reliable?' violates proper survey design principles because it is a
qs.e: A double-barreled question asks about two different issues in a single statement, confusing respondents and distorting results.

qs.q: A research student interviews 30 shoppers waiting at a bus stop simply because they are easy to reach and willing to answer questions quickly. This non-probability sampling method is
qs.e: Convenience sampling selects population members from whom it is easiest to obtain information.

qs.q: Testing a draft questionnaire on 25 respondents before deploying it to 2,000 respondents nationwide to detect confusing questions and timing issues is called
qs.e: Pre-testing (or pilot testing) involves administering a survey instrument to a small sub-sample to refine question wording and design.

qs.q: A fast-food restaurant in Abuja serves a customer cold fried chicken. When the customer complains, the manager replaces the meal immediately with a hot portion and provides a free drink coupon. This process of resolving service failure is
qs.e: Service recovery refers to the actions taken by a service provider in response to a service failure to restore customer satisfaction.

qs.q: A customer rates a commercial bank high on the SERVQUAL dimension of 'Empathy' when branch staff display
o: Caring, individualized attention to the customer's specific problems
qs.e: Empathy in SERVQUAL represents caring, individualized attention provided to customers.

qs.q: Mapping out step-by-step customer actions, visible front-stage employee interactions, and invisible back-stage support activities for a hotel check-in process creates a
qs.e: A service blueprint is a operational tool that visualizes the service delivery process across front-stage and back-stage touchpoints.

qs.q: A cinema management in Port Harcourt reduces ticket prices by 50% for Tuesday afternoon shows to fill empty seats during low-demand hours. This capacity management technique manages service
qs.e: Differential pricing during off-peak hours shifts consumer demand to match fixed capacity, overcoming service perishability.

qs.q: Commercial banks installing Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) and mobile banking applications to enable self-service cash withdrawals represent the deployment of
qs.e: Self-service technologies (SSTs) allow customers to produce a service independent of direct involvement by service firm employees.

qs.q: A commercial blog charges advertisers N50 per click whenever a reader clicks on an advert banner embedded in its blog articles. This digital pricing model is known as
o: Cost Per Click (CPC) / Pay Per Click (PPC)
qs.e: Cost Per Click (CPC) is an online advertising pricing model where the advertiser pays the publisher only when the ad is clicked.

qs.q: An online retail store tracks that 40 out of 100 website visitors leave the website immediately after viewing only the homepage without clicking any links. The homepage has a
qs.e: Bounce rate represents the percentage of visitors who enter the site and then leave ('bounce') rather than continuing to view other pages.

qs.q: A fashion brand sends customized email promotions containing discount coupon codes to users who added items to their digital shopping cart but closed the browser before paying. This technique is
