qs.e: Cart abandonment retargeting reaches out to prospective buyers who left items in an online cart to encourage them to complete the purchase.

qs.q: A wholesale spare parts dealer in Lagos creates a private online portal allowing registered motor mechanics across Nigeria to check stock levels, view trade prices, and place bulk orders. This operates under which business model?
qs.e: Business-to-Business (B2B) e-commerce involves digital commercial transactions between companies.

qs.q: An online business spends N500,000 on digital ads, attracting 20,000 clicks. From those clicks, 400 purchases are completed. What is the Cost Per Click (CPC) and the Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)?
qs.e: CPC = Total Spend / Total Clicks = N500,000 / 20,000 = N25. CAC = Total Spend / Total Purchases = N500,000 / 400 = N1,250.

qs.q: During which stage of the product lifecycle are industry profits at their peak level, attracting numerous competitor entry into the market?
qs.e: Profits peak in the late growth / early maturity stage as volume expanded rapidly while unit production costs declined due to economies of scale.

qs.q: A firm marketing a mature product in Nigeria decides to cut all promotional expenditures to minimum maintenance levels to maximize short-term cash flow while sales gradually drop. This strategy is
qs.e: Harvesting involves reducing costs (R&D, ad spend, maintenance) to increase short-term cash flows despite declining sales.

qs.q: Early adopters of a newly launched high-tech agricultural drone in Nigeria are characterized as being
o: Opinion leaders who adopt new ideas early but carefully
Skeptical consumers who adopt only after majority adoption
qs.e: Early adopters are opinion leaders who embrace new technologies early and guide mainstream buyer perceptions.

qs.q: A fashion item experiences an immediate, sudden spike in sales volume due to viral social media trend status, followed by an equally rapid collapse in sales within three months. The lifecycle curve of this item is a
qs.e: A fad is a temporary period of unusually high sales driven by consumer enthusiasm and immediate product or brand popularity.

qs.q: When a pharmaceutical company finds that its mature anti-malarial drug can also be marketed as a preventative treatment for travelers, it extends the product lifecycle through
o: Finding new product uses / Market modification
qs.e: Finding new product uses or new user segments expands the target market and extends the product lifecycle.

qs.q: In an industrial purchasing department, the senior engineering specialist who reviews technical blueprints and sets chemical purity standards for raw materials acts as an
qs.e: Influencers affect the buying decision by helping define specifications and providing technical information for evaluating alternatives.

qs.q: A manufacturing company buying a complex multi-million Naira automated bottling plant for the first time faces high risk and extensive technical evaluation. This organizational purchase situation is a
qs.e: A new task buy is a business buying situation in which the buyer purchases a product or service for the first time.

qs.q: Assigning dedicated senior key account managers to maintain direct personal relationships with a commercial bank's top 20 corporate accounts is an example of
qs.e: Key Account Management (KAM) focuses resources on building long-term strategic relationships with the company's most important business accounts.

qs.q: A software company maintains a central Customer Relationship Management (CRM) database recording purchase history, complaint logs, and renewal dates for all enterprise clients. The primary objective of CRM is to
o: Maximize customer retention and lifetime customer value
qs.e: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) manages detailed information about individual customers to maximize customer loyalty and lifetime value.

qs.q: Organized business buyers tend to differ from final individual consumers because organizational buyers typically feature
o: Fewer but much larger buyers with professional purchasing procedures
More numerous small buyers who buy impulsively
Geographically scattered buyers making small purchases
qs.e: Business markets usually contain far fewer but much larger buyers who follow formal procurement processes.

qs.q: A firm in Ibadan sells surplus agricultural machinery to a trading export merchant in Lagos, who then resells the machinery to buyers in Benin Republic without the Ibadan firm dealing directly with foreign buyers. This mode is
qs.e: Indirect exporting involves selling to domestic intermediaries who then export the product overseas.

qs.q: A multinational firm builds a wholly owned manufacturing factory in Ogun State, Nigeria, retaining 100% equity ownership and operational control. This international entry strategy is
qs.e: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) involves direct ownership of foreign-based manufacturing or assembly facilities.

qs.q: A country imposes a maximum statutory limit of 10,000 metric tons on the total quantity of foreign cement that can be imported into its territory per year. This trade barrier is an import
qs.e: An import quota is a limit placed on the amount of a product that can be imported into a country.

qs.q: A mobile phone manufacturer sells the exact same phone model with identical packaging and advertising worldwide without any regional alterations. This strategy is international product
qs.e: Product standardization markets the same product using the same marketing strategy worldwide.

qs.q: A shoes manufacturer in Aba exports leather boots to Ghana with a C.I.F. value of N20,000 per pair. If Ghana imposes a 20% import tariff duty, what is the landed cost per pair before local dealer margins?
qs.e: Landed cost = C.I.F value + Tariff duty = N20,000 + (20% of N20,000) = N20,000 + N4,000 = N24,000.

qs.q: A financial technology startup in Lagos develops a micro-investment mobile application based on extensive survey data showing young professionals want automated spare-change savings. By aligning product design directly with expressed user needs, the startup demonstrates the
qs.e: The marketing concept focuses on identifying customer needs first and designing products to satisfy those needs efficiently.

qs.q: A cement manufacturer in Ibese updates its kiln technology to reduce carbon emissions by 40% while donating solar streetlights to surrounding villages. Balancing company profitability, customer satisfaction, and long-term environmental protection embodies the
qs.e: The societal marketing concept balances company profits, consumer wants, and long-term public welfare.

qs.q: A fast-moving consumer goods company in Agbara restructures its distribution by replacing large central warehouses with regional fulfillment centers, reducing delivery transit time to retailers from 4 days to 24 hours. In the 4 Cs framework, this improves
qs.e: Convenience in the 4 Cs framework represents place and distribution efficiency, making products easily accessible to buyers.

qs.q: A private hospital in Abuja upgrades its reception ambiance, installs digital patient queue monitors, and provides branded comfort kits to admitted patients. In service marketing, these tangible elements represent
qs.e: Physical evidence includes tangible facilities, equipment, and visual elements that communicate service quality.

qs.q: A beverage producer in Benin City sells bottled natural spring water. To expand its portfolio, it introduces sparkling flavored water in 330ml aluminum cans. This new offering within the beverage category is a
qs.e: Line extension involves introducing new variants (flavors, packaging, sizes) within an existing product line.

qs.q: An industrial manufacturing plant in Kano purchases heavy hydraulic press machinery valued at N85,000,000 for its metal stamping operations. In industrial product classification, this machinery is a
qs.e: Capital items include major installations and machinery that aid in long-term manufacturing operations.

qs.q: A supermarket chain in Ibadan packages cassava flour under its own retail store brand, selling it at a lower price than national packaged flour brands. This product is a
qs.e: Private label (store) brands are owned and sold exclusively by a retailer or wholesaler.

qs.q: A famous biscuit brand in Nigeria uses its established brand name to launch a new line of breakfast cornflakes. This branding move is an example of
qs.e: Brand extension applies an existing brand name to enter a completely new product category.

qs.q: A milk powder manufacturer packages powdered milk into single-serve 12g sachets priced at N50, making high-quality milk accessible to low-income households daily. This packaging innovation utilizes
qs.e: Sachetization breaks bulk products into affordable micro-units tailored to daily consumer cash flows.

qs.q: A cosmetics manufacturer in Ogun State uses corrugated fiberboard master boxes to pack 48 individual shampoo bottles for truck transport to regional distributors. These master boxes represent
qs.e: Secondary packaging groups primary packages together for storage, retail handling, and shelf display.

qs.q: A trader in Alaba International Market, Lagos, purchases home theater systems for N40,000 each and applies a 30% markup on cost. What is the retail selling price?
qs.e: Selling price = Cost + (Cost x Markup %) = N40,000 + (N40,000 x 0.30) = N40,000 + N12,000 = N52,000.

qs.q: A retailer sells an electronic gadget for N25,000, achieving a profit of N5,000. What is the profit margin percentage on selling price, and what is the equivalent markup percentage on cost?
qs.e: Margin = Profit / Selling Price = N5,000 / N25,000 = 20%. Cost = N20,000. Markup = Profit / Cost = N5,000 / N20,000 = 25%.

qs.q: A manufacturing firm in Kaduna has fixed costs of N3,000,000 annually. It sells product X for N5,000 per unit with variable production costs of N2,000 per unit. What is the break-even sales volume in units and in Naira revenue?
qs.e: Contribution margin = N5,000 - N2,000 = N3,000. BEP units = N3,000,000 / N3,000 = 1,000 units. BEP revenue = 1,000 x N5,000 = N5,000,000.

qs.q: A publisher sells textbooks with a list price of N10,000, subject to a trade discount of 25% to booksellers and a 4% cash discount for payment within 14 days. If a bookseller pays within 14 days, what is the net price per book?
qs.e: Price after trade discount = N10,000 x 0.75 = N7,500. Cash discount = 4% of N7,500 = N300. Net price = N7,500 - N300 = N7,200.

qs.q: A solar energy firm in Enugu incurs fixed costs of N4,000,000 annually. Its solar home kit sells for N200,000 with variable costs of N120,000 per unit. To earn a target annual net profit of N2,000,000, how many units must be sold?
qs.e: CM per unit = N200,000 - N120,000 = N80,000. Required units = (Fixed Costs + Target Profit) / CM = (N4,000,000 + N2,000,000) / N80,000 = N6,000,000 / N80,000 = 75 units.

qs.q: A soft drink bottling company in Port Harcourt distributes through exclusive regional master distributors, who sell to sub-wholesalers, who then supply local retail kiosks. How many levels of intermediaries are in this distribution channel?
qs.e: The channel includes Master Distributor -> Sub-wholesaler -> Retail Kiosk, which equals three levels of intermediaries.

qs.q: A manufacturer of high-end luxury wristwatches appoints only two exclusive retail outlets in Lagos State to represent the brand. This distribution strategy is
qs.e: Exclusive distribution limits distribution to very few dealers with exclusive rights in specific territories.

qs.q: A conflict occurring between two authorized regional distributors of the same beer brand over selling into each other's allocated territories is categorized as
qs.e: Horizontal channel conflict occurs among firms at the same level of the channel (e.g. distributor vs distributor).

qs.q: A pharmaceutical manufacturer offers trade discounts and promotional displays to community pharmacy owners to encourage them to stock and recommend its new multivitamin brand. This strategy is a
qs.e: A push strategy directs marketing efforts at channel members to induce them to carry and push the product to end users.

qs.q: A company running a nationwide promotion spend allocation sets its budget by allocating 6% of its forecasted sales revenue of N1,500,000,000. What is the total promotional budget?
A radio advert broadcast in Kano costs N180,000 per 30-second slot and reaches an estimated audience of 600,000 listeners. What is the Cost Per Thousand (CPM) of this radio ad?
qs.e: CPM = (Ad Cost / Total Audience) x 1,000 = (N180,000 / 600,000) x 1,000 = N300.

qs.q: An established detergent brand runs short TV commercials showing clean white shirts with its catchy jingle without detailed product explanations. This represents
qs.e: Reminder advertising keeps the product top-of-mind for mature brands.

qs.q: A sales representative in Lagos earns a base salary of N120,000 plus a 6% commission on sales exceeding a monthly threshold of N3,000,000. If total monthly sales are N5,500,000, what is the total earnings?
qs.e: Commissionable sales = N5,500,000 - N3,000,000 = N2,500,000. Commission = 6% of N2,500,000 = N150,000. Total earnings = N120,000 + N150,000 = N270,000.

qs.q: A salesperson handling prospective industrial clients in Enugu researches company executive backgrounds and past equipment purchases prior to initiating contact. This stage in selling is
qs.e: Pre-approach involves conducting background research on prospective buyers before meeting them.

qs.q: A fast-food chain in Abuja attaches a scratch card to every meal deal, giving customers a chance to instantly win free drinks or cinema tickets. This promotional technique is a
qs.e: Contests and sweepstakes give consumers a chance to win prizes based on chance or skill.

qs.q: A detergent maker offers retail shopkeepers in Onitsha 2 extra free cartons for every 20 cartons purchased in a single order. This trade promotion is known as
qs.e: Free goods allowances provide extra product units at no charge to trade buyers meeting specific volume targets.

qs.q: An oil company operating in the Niger Delta builds schools, equips computer laboratories, and provides university scholarships for youths in its host communities. This program exemplifies
qs.e: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) builds long-term community goodwill and positive public relations.

qs.q: Following media reports about a minor batch defect, a food processing company voluntarily recalls the affected batch, issues a press statement, and opens a 24-hour helpline. This swift response is
qs.e: Crisis communications management handles emergency situations transparently to safeguard brand trust.

qs.q: A financial institution divides its consumer market into 'Recent University Graduates', 'Middle-Aged Executives', and 'Retirees' to offer customized pension and investment plans. This segmentation basis is
qs.e: Demographic lifecycle segmentation divides markets based on age cohorts and life stages.

qs.q: An athletic shoe brand designs distinct shoes for marathon runners, basketball players, and casual weekend walkers based on activity lifestyle. This market division relies on
qs.e: Psychographic (lifestyle) and behavioral (product usage) criteria segment consumers according to activities and specific benefit needs.

qs.q: A consumer experiences intense regret after purchasing a luxury car, questioning whether they spent too much money. This psychological state is known as
qs.e: Cognitive dissonance is post-purchase anxiety or doubt regarding a major buying decision.

qs.q: When purchasing cooking salt at a local store, a buyer picks the first package available without comparing brands or prices. This decision process exemplifies
qs.e: Habitual buying behavior involves low involvement and minimal brand differentiation.

qs.q: A market research team in Lagos gathers existing company sales reports, central bank economic bulletins, and published industry whitepapers prior to conducting field interviews. This data is classified as
qs.e: Secondary data is pre-existing data gathered previously for another purpose.

qs.q: A research group conducts structured discussions with 8 selected mothers in Kano led by a moderator to explore opinions on a new infant food formulation. This research method is a
qs.e: Focus group interviews gather qualitative insights from small groups guided by a moderator.

qs.q: An unsold seat on a commercial flight from Abuja to Lagos cannot be saved in inventory for sale on the following day's flight. This illustrates service
qs.e: Perishability means services cannot be stored for future sale.

qs.q: A patient receiving a medical consultation cannot physically touch or inspect the doctor's diagnosis prior to the service encounter. This characteristic is service
qs.e: Intangibility means services cannot be perceived by physical senses before purchase.

qs.q: An e-commerce business in Yaba spends N300,000 on digital ad banners, generating 15,000 ad clicks that result in 300 completed sales orders. What is the conversion rate and the Cost Per Click (CPC)?
Optimizing website code, keyword structure, and loading speed so a company ranks naturally at the top of Google organic search results is called
qs.e: Search Engine Optimization (SEO) improves organic, unpaid search engine visibility.

qs.q: A newly launched solar air-conditioner brand in Nigeria experiences high initial promotional costs, negative net operating profits, and slow initial sales growth. The product is in the
qs.e: The introduction stage features high launch expenditures, low initial sales volume, and negative profits.

qs.q: A digital streaming platform experiences rapid customer adoption, expanding sales revenues, rising operating profits, and entry of new market competitors. The product is in the
qs.e: The growth stage exhibits rapid sales expansion, profit growth, and competitive entry.

qs.q: Demand for industrial cocoa processing machinery in Ondo depends directly on consumer demand for packaged chocolate and cocoa beverages. In business marketing, this is
qs.e: Derived demand in B2B markets originates from ultimate consumer demand for end products.

qs.q: An administrative executive in a corporate purchasing department screens sales phone calls and prevents vendors from directly contacting the Procurement Manager. In buying center roles, the executive acts as a
qs.e: Gatekeepers control access to decision makers and manage the flow of information in a buying center.

qs.q: A Nigerian restaurant brand expands into Kenya by licensing a local operator in Nairobi to use its trade name, brand identity, and proprietary recipes in return for royalties. This entry mode is
qs.e: Franchising grants an independent operator the right to run a business under the franchisor's brand and system.

qs.q: A shoe manufacturer in Aba partners with a Ghanaian distribution company to co-establish a footwear factory in Accra, sharing equity investment and risks. This market entry mode is a
qs.e: A joint venture is a partnership where two firms create a jointly owned commercial entity, sharing equity and management.

qs.q: A global beverage corporation modifies its product line in West Africa by introducing a local hibiscus (zobo) flavor variant while maintaining its global brand umbrella. This strategy represents
qs.e: Glocalization (product adaptation) adapts global product strategies to local cultural preferences and market conditions.

qs.q: A manufacturer exports industrial water pumps to Cote d'Ivoire at a C.I.F. price of N50,000 per unit. If Cote d'Ivoire levies a 15% import tariff duty, what is the duty-inclusive landed cost per pump?
qs.e: Landed cost = C.I.F price + Tariff duty = N50,000 + (15% of N50,000) = N50,000 + N7,500 = N57,500.

qs.q: An industrial paper processing mill in Lagos faces fixed costs of N5,000,000 annually. Variable costs per ton of paper are N150,000 and selling price is N250,000 per ton. How many tons must be sold to break even?
qs.e: Contribution margin per ton = N250,000 - N150,000 = N100,000. BEP in tons = Fixed Costs / CM = N5,000,000 / N100,000 = 50 tons.

qs.q: A digital ad campaign spent N400,000 to generate 10,000 visits and 200 online purchases. Calculate the Cost Per Acquisition (CAC) and the website conversion rate.
qs.e: CAC = Total Spend / Purchases = N400,000 / 200 = N2,000. Conversion Rate = (200 / 10,000) x 100 = 2.0%.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant has annual fixed expenses of N6,000,000, variable costs of N12,000 per unit, and sells its product for N20,000 per unit. If annual sales volume is 1,200 units, what is the net margin percentage on total revenue?
qs.e: Total Revenue = 1,200 x N20,000 = N24,000,000. Total Variable Cost = 1,200 x N12,000 = N14,400,000. Contribution Margin = N9,600,000. Net Profit = CM - Fixed Expenses = N9,600,000 - N6,000,000 = N3,600,000. Net Margin = (N3,600,000 / N24,000,000) x 100 = 15.0%.

qs.q: A retail supermarket in Port Harcourt buys canned soup for N600 per can and sets a selling price of N800. What is the markup percentage on cost and the margin percentage on selling price?
qs.e: Profit = N800 - N600 = N200. Markup on cost = N200 / N600 = 33.33%. Margin on selling price = N200 / N800 = 25.0%.
